az:HB 2013.title: exceptional events; air quality; wildfires
az:HB 2013.summary: Requires the Department of Environmental Quality to submit an exceptional event demonstration to the U.S. EPA when a wildfire over 25,000 acres on federally managed land affects Arizona through smoke or land damage.

az:HB 2015.title: budget procedures; late filing penalty
az:HB 2015.summary: Sets penalties for organizations that fail to submit accurate financial statements to the Department of Administration for federal single audits, capped each fiscal year at $8 million or 1 percent of their General Fund appropriation.

az:HB 2028.title: DWR; application; administrative completeness
az:HB 2028.summary: Allows a court to order an indigent defendant experiencing homelessness to perform community restitution instead of paying the $20 assessment deposited in the Judicial Collection Enhancement Fund.

az:HB 2047.title: writ of restitution; criminal trespass
az:HB 2047.summary: Makes it first-degree rather than third-degree criminal trespass for a person served with a writ of restitution after an eviction to remain in or return to the property.

az:HB 2086.title: vaccination mandates; masks; prohibition
az:HB 2086.summary: Bars government entities from requiring Arizona residents to wear masks or face coverings, and extends the existing ban on government vaccine mandates from COVID-19 to any disease or virus.

az:HB 2113.title: public service corporation; rates; intervenor
az:HB 2113.summary: Requires the Residential Utility Consumer Office director to intervene in a utility rate case when the proposed increase to residential customers is 100 percent or more.

az:HB 2118.title: mobile food vendors; licensure
az:HB 2118.summary: Bars cities and towns from requiring mobile food vendors to obtain a local regulatory permit or license, and removes the allowance for local licenses requiring background checks or identification.

az:HB 2134.title: critical infrastructure; foreign adversaries; prohibition
az:HB 2134.summary: Bars use of software and communications equipment from Chinese companies in Arizona critical infrastructure, overrides contracts allowing foreign access or control, and sets certification, reporting and publication requirements.

az:HB 2140.title: bullion depository; state monies; treasurer
az:HB 2140.summary: Allows the State Treasurer to invest up to 10 percent of state trust and treasury monies in physical gold or silver bullion held in a U.S. commercial depository meeting security, insurance and audit standards.

az:HB 2170.title: state contracts; foreign adversary; prohibition
az:HB 2170.summary: Bars companies domiciled in China and controlled by its government, military or ruling party from state contracts for electronic or information technology, requires bidders to certify they are not domiciled in China, and sets a $100,000 civil penalty for false certification.

az:HB 2174.title: insurance; modeling organizations; predictive models
az:HB 2174.summary: Renames advisory organizations as model and data organizations, applies the same rules to them, and removes the insurance director's authority to examine them.

az:HB 2244.title: evictions; satisfaction of judgments
az:HB 2244.summary: Sets that if a landlord does not respond within 15 days to a tenant's motion to compel satisfaction of an eviction judgment, the filing fee is waived, no hearing is held, and the judgment is deemed satisfied on proof of payment.

az:HB 2249.title: parents' bill of rights; remedies
az:HB 2249.summary: Adds to the Parents' Bill of Rights the right to consent to and be informed of school social transitioning of a minor and to access the child's full education record, and sets liability and remedies for violations.

az:HB 2257.title: HOV lane; blood transport vehicles
az:HB 2257.summary: Changes the split of watercraft registration fees to 55 percent (was 65) for the Watercraft Licensing Fund, and sets fixed county percentages for the Law Enforcement and Boating Safety Fund in place of a Game and Fish Commission formula.

az:HB 2279.title: commercial river outfitters; limited liability
az:HB 2279.summary: Gives commercial river outfitters in Grand Canyon National Park immunity from claims arising out of a river trip's inherent risks, and from ordinary negligence claims waived in a liability release; does not cover gross negligence or willful acts.

az:HB 2379.title: school district governing boards; training
az:HB 2379.summary: Requires each school district governing board member to complete school finance training within 45 days after their term begins, and sets requirements for the training program.

az:HB 2380.title: school districts; board meetings; expenditures
az:HB 2380.summary: Requires school district boards to hold meetings at a public facility in the district and give public access to meeting materials and recordings, lets members pull items from consent agendas, and sets rules for approving out-of-state travel.

az:HB 2482.title: building renewal grants; procurement practices
az:HB 2482.summary: Caps individual job orders at $1 million for non-emergency construction projects funded by Building Renewal Grant monies, and requires the School Facilities Division to verify that projects are not split to avoid the cap.

az:HB 2502.title: ASRS; retirement; elected officials
az:HB 2502.summary: Lets an elected official who has reached normal retirement date retire from the state retirement system without resigning from office, and requires the employer to pay the alternate contribution rate.

az:HB 2592.title: artificial intelligence; state agencies; rules
az:HB 2592.summary: Requires state budget units to identify uses of artificial intelligence that reduce administrative burdens, eliminate regulations that unnecessarily restrict AI innovation and streamline AI procurement, and requires the Department of Administration to report annually by December 1.

az:HB 2660.title: health boards; licensure decisions; investigation
az:HB 2660.summary: Requires a health professional charged with a crime to stop practicing after a detrimental board licensing decision; otherwise stays the board's action pending appeal. Sets what the board must file with the Office of Administrative Hearings within 30 days.

az:HB 2661.title: parents' rights; guardianship; notice; attestation
az:HB 2661.summary: Adds to the rights of parents or guardians under a Department of Child Safety abuse or neglect investigation the right to be told they may delegate temporary guardianship of the child.

az:HB 2662.title: parenting time; expert testimony; qualifications
az:HB 2662.summary: Allows a court in a parenting-time case involving alleged domestic violence or abuse to hear expert testimony only from witnesses with clinical experience working with victims, and limits the psychological methods experts may use to empirically established ones.

az:HB 2745.title: legislative subpoena; perjury; refusal; contempt
az:HB 2745.summary: Lets the Senate President, Speaker or a committee chairperson issue an order holding a witness in contempt for ignoring a legislative subpoena, after notice and an opportunity for a hearing, and allows a county sheriff to arrest the witness.

az:HB 2762.title: food products; labeling; cultivated cells
az:HB 2762.summary: Requires labels reading cell-cultivated or cell-cultured on food products derived from cultivated cells, placed by the manufacturer, packager or retailer.

az:HB 2763.title: shooting range; closure; conditions
az:HB 2763.summary: Adds a condition to closing a shooting range: the Legislature must adopt a joint resolution approving the Game and Fish Commission's closure.

az:HB 2771.title: community supervision; rehabilitation; costs
az:HB 2771.summary: Lets the Department of Corrections require, as a condition of community supervision, that a prisoner pay reasonable costs of participating in a rehabilitation program.

az:HB 2782.title: corporation commission; utilities; amortization; tariffs
az:HB 2782.summary: Requires the Corporation Commission and utilities to make disclosures when a regulatory asset is included in rate base or reflected in rates based on a test year or historical balance.

az:HB 2800.title: ignition interlock devices; violation; classification
az:HB 2800.summary: Increases the penalty for knowingly lending a vehicle without an ignition interlock device to a DUI-restricted driver who then causes a collision with serious injury or death.

az:HB 2830.title: fetal and prenatal development; instruction
az:HB 2830.summary: Requires the State Board of Education to adopt age-appropriate science standards that include instruction on fetal and prenatal human development.

az:HB 2874.title: campaign committees; termination statements; contributions
az:HB 2874.summary: Changes how late-filing penalties are assessed for campaign committees that file termination statements, letting treasurers certify the committee received no contributions. Applies retroactive to July 6, 2016, as an emergency measure.

az:HB 2941.title: motorcycles; reckless driving
az:HB 2941.summary: Classifies riding a motorcycle between lanes of traffic, or passing in the same lane, as reckless driving, a class 2 misdemeanor, except where authorized.

az:HB 2950.title: tourism improvement areas; municipalities; counties
az:HB 2950.summary: Allows cities and counties to create tourism improvement areas funded by assessments on lodging businesses, managed by a destination marketing organization, and sets procedures for formation petitions, hearings, assessments and dissolution.

az:HB 2970.title: fraudulent schemes; artifices; jurisdiction
az:HB 2970.summary: Provides that in fraudulent scheme prosecutions the state need not prove all unlawful acts happened in Arizona or one jurisdiction, and that this is no defense.

az:HB 4010.title: genetic counselors; board; licensure
az:HB 4010.summary: Creates the Board of Genetic Counselors to license and regulate genetic counselors, and requires practitioners to be licensed in Arizona no later than October 1, 2026.

az:HB 4018.title: technical correction; public records
az:HB 4018.summary: Lets a county sheriff use volunteer posse and reserve organizations and gives the sheriff exclusive authority to regulate their organization and equipment under written policy.

az:HB 4043.title: training; AEDs; CPR; school personnel
az:HB 4043.summary: Requires each school district and charter school campus to have, from August 1, 2027, at least one employee trained in CPR and first aid, and in AED use if the campus has one.

az:HB 4049.title: attorney general; legal counsel; exemption
az:HB 4049.summary: Lets the Department of Child Safety employ its own legal counsel, and requires the Attorney General to represent the state's interest, not the department, in child-welfare cases alleging department misconduct.

az:HB 4056.title: technical correction; double punishment
az:HB 4056.summary: Bars charging a legislator any fee for a public records request made in an official capacity, and requires the records be provided in any format the legislator requests.

az:SB 1011.title: medical examiners; sudden infant death
az:SB 1011.summary: Requires county medical examiners or forensic pathologists, in sudden and unexplained infant deaths, to review the infant's vaccination history from the prior 90 days and report the death to a national case registry.

az:SB 1013.title: public employees; merit; hiring practices
az:SB 1013.summary: Bars the state and its political subdivisions from adopting policies requiring hiring on any basis other than merit, or from influencing workforce composition by race, sex or similar characteristics.

az:SB 1015.title: gender transition procedures; provider liability
az:SB 1015.summary: Makes health professionals who provide gender transition procedures strictly liable for the costs of later detransition procedures, and lets a person who undergoes one, before turning 26, sue for those costs and attorney fees.

az:SB 1061.title: fentanyl; sale amount; nine grams
az:SB 1061.summary: Lowers from 200 grams to 9 grams the amount of fentanyl in a sale to another person that triggers specified criminal sentencing ranges.

az:SB 1068.title: disruption; educational institution; concealed weapon
az:SB 1068.summary: Bars public universities, colleges and community colleges from banning concealed weapon permit holders from carrying a concealed weapon, or banning the lawful transport or storage of a firearm, on campus.

az:SB 1069.title: prohibited weapons; muffling device; repeal
az:SB 1069.summary: Removes devices designed to muffle the sound of a firearm (silencers) from the state's definition of prohibited weapons.

az:SB 1075.title: foreign entities; land; legislative approval
az:SB 1075.summary: Bars sale, lease or sublease of Arizona land to a foreign entity hostile to the United States without Foreign Entity Review Commission approval, requires grantee identification be filed with the Department of Real Estate, and allows the Attorney General to seek civil penalties.

az:SB 1095.title: gender transition; minors; prohibitions
az:SB 1095.summary: Bars physicians and other health professionals from providing gender transition procedures to, or referring for them, anyone under 18, effective April 1, 2027.

az:SB 1121.title: radiation protection systems; medical procedures
az:SB 1121.summary: Bars hospitals from requiring health professionals to wear lead aprons during cardiac catheterization procedures using real-time x-ray when the room has a radiation protection system.

az:SB 1124.title: health boards; evaluations; notice
az:SB 1124.summary: Requires health profession regulatory boards to vote on and give 14 days' written notice, with a summary of the complaint, before ordering a psychological or psychiatric evaluation of a health professional, who may submit a written response.

az:SB 1133.title: candidate financial disclosures; public officers
az:SB 1133.summary: Deems a candidate to meet the financial disclosure requirement for nomination papers if they filed the annual public officer disclosure for that year. Emergency measure.

az:SB 1136.title: workers' compensation; death benefits; remarriage
az:SB 1136.summary: Lets the surviving spouse of a first responder keep receiving workers' compensation death benefits for life, including spouses who lost benefits through remarriage on or after January 1, 2000, going forward only.

az:SB 1164.title: ALTCS; providers; change of ownership
az:SB 1164.summary: Sets change-of-ownership procedures so licensed skilled nursing and assisted living facilities can keep processing claims for services to Arizona Long-Term Care System members.

az:SB 1167.title: cities; towns; counties; posting; website
az:SB 1167.summary: Lets cities, towns and counties meet legal notice advertising requirements by posting on their own website and the website of a qualified newspaper.

az:SB 1174.title: DCS; intake hotline; case history
az:SB 1174.summary: Requires, from January 1, 2027, the Department of Child Safety intake hotline to produce one report covering the full hotline and investigation history of a child and the child's siblings.

az:SB 1189.title: campaign spending; personal security
az:SB 1189.summary: Lets a candidate committee spend campaign money on the personal security of the candidate and family members.

az:SB 1206.title: storm related insurance claims
az:SB 1206.summary: Bars insurance adjusters and contractors from soliciting services while a loss-causing event or emergency response is active, and bars contractors from advertising or paying a policyholder's insurance deductible.

az:SB 1210.title: private postsecondary education; nondomiciled institutions
az:SB 1210.summary: Creates a separate registration process for private postsecondary schools based outside Arizona, setting the information they must submit to the state board.

az:SB 1212.title: health insurance; reimbursement rates; vaccines
az:SB 1212.summary: Bars health insurers, beginning January 1, 2027, from paying a health professional a different reimbursement rate because a covered patient refuses one or more vaccines.

az:SB 1215.title: firefighters; occupational disease; cancers
az:SB 1215.summary: Clarifies, retroactive to July 1, 2021, which conditions are presumed work-related for workers' compensation coverage of peace officers, firefighters and fire investigators.

az:SB 1221.title: tax laws; interpretation; application; hearing
az:SB 1221.summary: Requires the Department of Revenue to notify the Legislature before adopting a tax-law interpretation that adversely affects taxpayers, and to testify if the Legislature holds a hearing.

az:SB 1233.title: administrative deficiencies; cure period
az:SB 1233.summary: Bars the Department of Health Services, AHCCCS and Department of Economic Security from disciplining or taking enforcement action against a licensed or contracted facility with only administrative deficiencies unless the facility first gets 72 hours to cure them.

az:SB 1242.title: mental health; hearings; audiovisual technology
az:SB 1242.summary: Changes procedures for court-ordered mental health evaluation and treatment, including virtual hearings and testimony, and sets care-coordination requirements between treatment agencies and secure behavioral health residential facilities.

az:SB 1253.title: safe haven providers; hospital deliveries
az:SB 1253.summary: Lets a parent or agent surrender a newborn at the hospital of birth without first being discharged and later returning to complete the surrender.

az:SB 1259.title: campaigns; protected residential addresses
az:SB 1259.summary: Lets a person with a legally protected residential address give an alternate mailing address and attest to their residence when filing a committee organization statement or annual financial disclosure.

az:SB 1274.title: special plate; police foundation
az:SB 1274.summary: Creates a timeshare salesperson license, effective July 1, 2027, and sets licensure requirements and qualifications.

az:SB 1280.title: public monies; Mexican wolf; prohibition
az:SB 1280.summary: Bars the Game and Fish Commission from transporting Mexican gray wolf puppies into Arizona or using public money or resources to do so.

az:SB 1286.title: veterinarian visits; electronic means; prescriptions
az:SB 1286.summary: Changes the time periods in which a veterinarian may issue and renew prescriptions for certain drugs after an examination conducted by electronic means.

az:SB 1315.title: public schools; interoperable communications; requirements
az:SB 1315.summary: Requires school districts and charter schools that receive state or local law enforcement money for interoperable communications to maintain capabilities for notifying and communicating with local law enforcement in school emergencies, with reporting requirements.

az:SB 1318.title: mammography results; notice; repeal
az:SB 1318.summary: Repeals the requirement that health care facilities give patients identified as having heterogeneously dense or extremely dense breasts a specified notice.

az:SB 1327.title: ABOR; foreign countries; restrictions; penalties
az:SB 1327.summary: Requires the Board of Regents to have each public university adopt a research security policy to guard research against foreign influence, and sets required policy elements and reporting to the Board.

az:SB 1335.title: water banking; annual report; posting
az:SB 1335.summary: Lets a holder of groundwater savings credits keep irrigating the land under its former irrigation grandfathered right for up to two years after the credits are issued, under a temporary permit from the Department of Water Resources.

az:SB 1338.title: state; local public benefits; eligibility
az:SB 1338.summary: Removes the exclusion for state public retirement system benefits from the definition of state or local public benefit, and lists persons who are ineligible to receive any state or local public benefit.

az:SB 1345.title: health facilities; anonymous complaints; prohibition
az:SB 1345.summary: Sets timelines for the Department of Health Services to license health care institutions and to review third-party accreditation survey results, and lets it set initial licensing inspection fees by rule.

az:SB 1366.title: commercial buildings; telecommunications services
az:SB 1366.summary: Creates the Public Property Towing and Impound Practices Study Committee.

az:SB 1399.title: prepaid capitated contractors; cost reports
az:SB 1399.summary: Requires the state Medicaid agency (AHCCCS) to report to the Legislature and Governor each December 1 the share of money its prepaid managed-care contractors spend on provider payments and on categories of administrative costs.

az:SB 1419.title: solar energy; inspection; contractors
az:SB 1419.summary: Sets requirements for installing and inspecting solar energy devices, for distributed energy generation system agreements, and for disclosures in sales presentations and documents.

az:SB 1421.title: undocumented aliens; financial services
az:SB 1421.summary: Bars check cashers and financial institutions from accepting as identification licenses or ID cards issued only to unauthorized or undocumented immigrants, and bars remittance transfers to unauthorized aliens. Sets compliance and enforcement rules.

az:SB 1422.title: credit enhancement eligibility board; continuation
az:SB 1422.summary: Continues the Credit Enhancement Eligibility Board, which oversees the program guaranteeing financing for achievement district public schools, for 10 years, until July 1, 2036.

az:SB 1429.title: board of directors; commerce authority.
az:SB 1429.summary: Applies a strict compliance standard of review to city, town and county initiatives and referenda, and adds requirements for petition circulators.

az:SB 1445.title: water quality; testing; on-site
az:SB 1445.summary: Lets cities and towns of 1,000 to 9,999 people holding aquifer protection permits test bacteriological samples on-site with EPA-approved equipment, and bars the Department of Environmental Quality from requiring small community water systems to keep storage above 1,000 gallons.

az:SB 1452.title: cargo theft task force
az:SB 1452.summary: Creates the Cargo Theft Task Force, subject to legislative funding, to address cargo theft and related offenses, and sets its membership and reporting requirements.

az:SB 1475.title: interscholastic activities; criminal offenses; ineligibility
az:SB 1475.summary: Requires school district boards to bar students from school-sponsored interscholastic activities if convicted of, or admitting to, listed offenses such as aggravated assault, sex offenses, stalking and domestic violence, and to require students to certify whether they committed one.

az:SB 1477.title: assisted living facilities; referral agents
az:SB 1477.summary: Adds disclosure and insurance requirements for assisted living referral agencies.

az:SB 1494.title: technical correction; open pit mining
az:SB 1494.summary: Bars health care providers, institutions and drug manufacturers from paying enrollees' insurance premiums or steering them to change plans based on health status, and sets penalties.

az:SB 1497.title: classical learning; tests; examinations
az:SB 1497.summary: Requires school districts with a self-insurance program and at least 300 employees to obtain coverage quotes at least once every four years.

az:SB 1560.title: cap; water supply development fund
az:SB 1560.summary: Raises the cap on a single loan from the Water Supply Development Revolving Fund from $3 million to $20 million.

az:SB 1561.title: assisted living; notice; study committee
az:SB 1561.summary: Creates the Vulnerable Adult System Study Committee and requires assisted living discharge or eviction notices to include a statement of the resident's rights.

az:SB 1572.title: public schools; civics instruction requirement
az:SB 1572.summary: Requires each public school to observe Celebrate Freedom Week, with instruction on the Declaration of Independence and Constitution in social studies courses and a student recitation of a Declaration passage in grades 3-12. Sets exemptions and State Board of Education duties.

az:SB 1573.title: judicial determinations; religious sectarian laws
az:SB 1573.summary: Bars courts from relying on religious sectarian law as controlling or persuasive authority, including federal courts sitting in diversity, with exceptions for Anglo-American legal tradition and certain marriage recognitions.

az:SB 1620.title: Arizona space commission; board; membership
az:SB 1620.summary: Requires municipalities to set a reimbursement process for telecommunications utility facility relocation costs and to give 30 days' public notice of voter-approved bond projects before requesting relocation.

az:SB 1624.title: photo radar enforcement; civil penalty
az:SB 1624.summary: Caps the penalty for photo-enforcement traffic violations at $75 with exceptions, sends $15 to the Peace Officer Training Equipment Fund, and bars using such violations to set insurance or affect driving privileges.

az:SB 1711.title: age-appropriate resources; inappropriate contact; schools
az:SB 1711.summary: Requires the State Board of Education to compile recommended resources for age-appropriate education on recognizing and preventing inappropriate contact, and requires public schools to make them available to students and parents.

az:SB 1723.title: domestic violence; release conditions
az:SB 1723.summary: Requires judges to impose electronic monitoring, where available, as a release condition for people charged with a domestic violence offense causing physical harm, and lets a court require someone under an order of protection to give the plaintiff identifying information.

az:SB 1741.title: public schools; released time courses
az:SB 1741.summary: Requires school districts and charter schools to let students attend released time courses during the school day when set requirements are met, and lets adversely affected persons sue for violations.

az:SB 1814.title: substance use disorder treatment; committee
az:SB 1814.summary: Creates the Substance Use Disorder Treatment Standards and Oversight Study Committee to review treatment programs, access gaps, standards and funding needs, and sets its membership and reporting duties.

ia:HF 1028.title: A bill for an act relating to matters under the purview of the department of management, and including effective date and applicability provisions.
ia:HF 1028.summary: As introduced, changes technology reinvestment fund use, appropriating it to the Department of Management for technology projects with a prioritized project list for the governor, and moves other data and information technology duties to the department.

ia:HF 2200.title: A bill for an act relating to activities in the administration of alcoholic beverage control by the department of revenue, and including effective date provisions.
ia:HF 2200.summary: As introduced, limits alcoholic beverages commission members' ties to alcohol businesses, with no more than two having a financial interest, and bars members from promoting political views or candidates.

ia:HF 2254.title: A bill for an act relating to the prohibition of noncompete clauses in certain employment contracts entered into by the university of Iowa hospitals and clinics, and including effective date provisions.
ia:HF 2254.summary: As introduced, directs the Board of Regents to develop a policy barring University of Iowa Hospitals and Clinics from including noncompete clauses in physician contracts entered into, extended, or renewed after the bill takes effect.

ia:HF 2297.title: A bill for an act relating to radon mitigation in residential buildings.
ia:HF 2297.summary: As introduced, requires the state building code to require a passive radon mitigation system in new single-family and two-family homes, using methods listed in the 2021 International Residential Code.

ia:HF 2329.title: A bill for an act relating to interest rates and charges on regulated loans, and consumer credit transaction service charges.
ia:HF 2329.summary: As introduced, sets the interest rate and charges for all regulated loans at 3 percent per month, ending the superintendent of banking's authority to redetermine maximum rates, and raises the consumer credit service charge cap from $30 to $100.

ia:HF 2337.title: A bill for an act relating to fraudulent practices involving academic credentials or professional or occupational licenses, and making penalties applicable.
ia:HF 2337.summary: As introduced, makes it a class D felony, punishable by up to five years in prison, to falsely claim an academic degree or credentials to get a job or other personal gain.

ia:HF 2490.title: A bill for an act relating to public meetings and records, including public notice requirements for meetings of a governmental body, supervision and fees associated with examining and copying public records, employment separation information for certain government employees, contractors, or appointees, and injunctions to restrain vexatious requesters.
ia:HF 2490.summary: As introduced, requires governmental bodies to give meeting notice by posting it prominently and on any associated website, and to mark amended agendas "AMENDED" and issue a new notice.

ia:HF 2493.title: A bill for an act relating to the statewide preschool program by modifying provisions relating to eligibility, funding, and compulsory attendance and including applicability provisions.
ia:HF 2493.summary: As introduced, extends the state preschool program and its funding to five-year-olds who turn five between March 15 and September 15, starting with school budget years beginning July 1, 2027.

ia:HF 2501.title: A bill for an act relating to the conduct of elections.
ia:HF 2501.summary: As introduced, changes election laws, including requiring investigators of election misconduct to notify the state elections commissioner, canceling incomplete voter registrations that are not resolved, and changing public measure recount rules.

ia:HF 2514.title: A bill for an act making children of child care workers in this state eligible for the state child care assistance program.
ia:HF 2514.summary: As introduced, makes children of child care workers eligible for state child care assistance if the parent works an average of at least 32 hours weekly providing child care at a participating facility, with copayments set by rule.

ia:HF 2523.title: A bill for an act establishing the right of a parent or guardian of a minor child to consent to and authorize certain medical services over the minor child’s objection.
ia:HF 2523.summary: As introduced, allows a parent, guardian, or custodian to have a child committed for substance use or mental health treatment over the child's objection, without the court order currently required.

ia:HF 2531.title: A bill for an act relating to interests in minerals owned by counties and cities, and including effective date provisions.
ia:HF 2531.summary: As introduced, requires counties and cities to convey mineral interests they own to the surface landowner within five years, and lets counties convey delinquent-tax mineral interests to the landowner if the owner does not pay within 90 days of notice.

ia:HF 2542.title: A bill for an act relating to habitual offenders, and providing penalties.
ia:HF 2542.summary: As introduced, rewrites Iowa's habitual offender law so a person is a habitual offender after accumulating three or more points from prior convictions, with points assigned by offense level.

ia:HF 2602.title: A bill for an act relating to the licensure of massage establishments, and making penalties applicable.
ia:HF 2602.summary: As introduced, requires massage therapy establishments to hold a license starting January 1, 2027, with applications to the Board of Massage Therapy and possible sanitary inspections.

ia:HF 2615.title: A bill for an act relating to thoroughbred and quarter horse racing seasons.
ia:HF 2615.summary: As introduced, requires thoroughbred and quarter horse racing seasons to be separate, non-overlapping meets, unless the breed associations and the Polk County track licensee agree in writing to mixed meets.

ia:HF 2617.title: A bill for an act relating to abandoned vehicles.
ia:HF 2617.summary: As introduced, rewrites and reorganizes the Code section on towing, impounding, reclaiming and selling abandoned vehicles, including notice requirements, without changing its substance, and defines "garagekeeper".

ia:HF 2635.title: A bill for an act relating to health carriers standards of conduct; utilization review organizations, artificial intelligence, audits, and prior authorizations; certificate of need processes; and including applicability provisions.
ia:HF 2635.summary: As introduced, sets claim payment deadlines of 30 days (electronic) or 45 days (paper) for health insurers, limits retroactive denials, requires reimbursing providers' audit costs, and changes prior authorization and utilization review rules.

ia:HF 2667.title: A bill for an act relating to project design standards and specifications, including by providing for a statewide urban design and specifications board and requiring certain reports to city councils regarding noncompliant projects.
ia:HF 2667.summary: As introduced, creates a statewide urban design and specifications board within the Department of Transportation to publish design and specifications manuals, and makes a city or county pay added costs for projects it approves that do not comply with the manuals.

ia:HF 2670.title: A bill for an act relating to education, including by modifying provisions related to summative testing in schools and the educational program provided to students enrolled in kindergarten through grade twelve, and including applicability provisions.
ia:HF 2670.summary: As introduced, changes school testing and curriculum rules, requiring the state board to set core academic indicators in social studies for grades 8 and 10 and requiring a social studies assessment for students in those grades.

ia:HF 2676.title: A bill for an act relating to health-related matters, including health-related professions, nutrition, medication, and education, and including effective date and applicability provisions.
ia:HF 2676.summary: As introduced, changes health regulation, including requiring nutrition and metabolic health continuing education for some licensees and changing certificate of need definitions, along with other health professions, facilities, and tax provisions.

ia:HF 2694.title: A bill for an act relating to the regulation of certain places and activities by the governor.
ia:HF 2694.summary: As introduced, prohibits the governor from closing, mandating conditions on, or otherwise regulating places of worship for any reason, including during a disaster emergency or public health disaster.

ia:HF 2706.title: A bill for an act relating to judicial officers, including magistrate appointments in judicial election districts, senior magistrates, and judicial officer compensation, and including effective date provisions.
ia:HF 2706.summary: As introduced, changes judicial officer rules, including appointing magistrates by judicial election district instead of by county, and addressing senior magistrates and judicial officer compensation.

ia:HF 2707.title: A bill for an act relating to alignment of delivery of health and human services programs and services, aging and disability services, and volunteer services, and including applicability and effective date provisions.
ia:HF 2707.summary: As introduced, changes health and human services programs, including directing the department to divide the state into health and human services districts that initially match the behavioral health districts.

ia:HF 2724.title: A bill for an act requiring the board of educational examiners to establish additional endorsements and authorizations.
ia:HF 2724.summary: As introduced, requires the board of educational examiners to adopt fine arts, math and science teaching endorsements that require a bachelor's degree, and a K-12 instructional strategist II endorsement that does not require a master's degree.

ia:HF 2757.title: A bill for an act relating to nuclear electric generation facilities by creating sales and use tax exemptions and refunds, making appropriations to the state board of regents for establishing and maintaining a nuclear energy workforce, making penalties applicable, and including applicability and retroactive applicability provisions.
ia:HF 2757.summary: As introduced, exempts property and services used to build, restart, repair, or maintain nuclear electric generation facilities that start or restart on or after January 1, 2028, from state sales and use tax.

ia:HF 2766.title: A bill for an act relating to captive insurance companies and life captive reinsurance companies, and including civil penalties.
ia:HF 2766.summary: As introduced, makes tax returns on gross premiums filed by insurance and captive insurance companies confidential, making it a serious misdemeanor for current or former state employees to publish them.

ia:HF 2768.title: A bill for an act relating to and making appropriations for state government administration and regulation, including the department of administrative services, auditor of state, ethics and campaign disclosure board, offices of governor and lieutenant governor, department of inspections, appeals, and licensing, department of insurance and financial services, department of management, Iowa public employees’ retirement system, public information board, department of revenue, secretary of state, treasurer of state, and utilities commission.
ia:HF 2768.summary: As introduced, appropriates state money for fiscal year 2026-2027 to general government agencies, including the auditor, governor's office, revenue, insurance, secretary of state, treasurer, and utilities commission.

ia:HF 2770.title: A bill for an act relating to and making appropriations to the justice system, providing fees, and including applicability provisions.
ia:HF 2770.summary: As introduced, appropriates state money for fiscal year 2026-2027 to the justice system, including the departments of justice, corrections, public safety and public defense, the law enforcement academy, and the state public defender.

ia:HF 2771.title: A bill for an act relating to and making appropriations involving state government entities associated with agriculture, natural resources, and environmental protection, and including contingent effective date provisions.
ia:HF 2771.summary: As introduced, appropriates state money for fiscal year 2026-2027 to the departments of agriculture and natural resources and to agricultural and environmental programs at Iowa State University and the University of Iowa.

ia:HF 2779.title: A bill for an act relating to authorizations to conduct advance deposit wagering.
ia:HF 2779.summary: As introduced, requires the racing and gaming commission to authorize entities meeting simulcasting licensure rules to run advance deposit wagering, and bars such wagers within five miles of a racetrack without the track's agreement.

ia:HF 2780.title: A bill for an act relating to alcoholic beverage control by providing for certificates of compliance and the issuance of class “A” wine permits to nonnative wine manufacturers, permitting cities to create social districts for the consumption of alcoholic beverages, and providing fees.
ia:HF 2780.summary: As introduced, changes alcohol regulation by removing the distiller's certificate requirement for some brand resellers and allowing class A wine permits for out-of-state wine makers.

ia:HF 2781.title: A bill for an act relating to allocations of moneys from the juvenile detention home fund.
ia:HF 2781.summary: As introduced, changes how the juvenile detention home fund is divided, giving each home $150,000 first and sharing the rest based on each home's share of the prior year's costs.

ia:HF 2785.title: A bill for an act extending the biodiesel blended fuel tax credit.
ia:HF 2785.summary: As introduced, extends the repeal date of the biodiesel blended fuel tax credit for retail dealers from January 1, 2028, to January 1, 2033, for individual and corporate income taxes.

ia:HF 2786.title: A bill for an act modifying the sales or use tax refund for biodiesel production.
ia:HF 2786.summary: As introduced, raises the sales or use tax refund for biodiesel producers to 5 cents per gallon produced in Iowa and moves the refund's repeal date from January 1, 2028, to January 1, 2031.

ia:HF 2787.title: A bill for an act prohibiting warrant resolution clinics, including enforcement mechanisms, providing penalties, and including effective date provisions.
ia:HF 2787.summary: As introduced, bans warrant resolution clinics, which are events outside regular court proceedings that let people with outstanding arrest warrants resolve them without immediate arrest, and sets enforcement measures.

ia:HF 2788.title: A bill for an act relating to abortions including definitions, informed consent, dispensing of abortion-inducing drugs, and other abortion-related provisions.
ia:HF 2788.summary: As introduced, changes abortion rules, requiring an in-person physician exam and a signed patient agreement before abortion-inducing drugs are prescribed, and requiring reporting of complications from those drugs.

ia:HF 2799.title: A bill for an act relating to matters under the purview of the economic development authority, the utilities commission, and the department of education, including creation of the headquarters expansion and development for growth and employment program, and the business incentives for growth program training fund; repeal of the new jobs tax credit program; the major economic growth attraction program; load forecasting and analysis of electric transmission system expansion plans; creation of the electric transmission system expansion planning and analysis and load forecasting fund; the industrial new jobs training program; and establishing the new jobs training program interim study committee; and including effective date provisions.
ia:HF 2799.summary: As introduced, creates a business tax incentive program for headquarters expansion and job growth, and makes changes to economic development programs, electric transmission planning and load forecasting, and the industrial new jobs training program.

ia:HF 2800.title: A bill for an act relating to state and local government and finances, including by making, modifying, limiting, or reducing appropriations, distributions, or transfers, authorizing expenditure of unappropriated moneys in special funds, making corrections, and providing for properly related matters including the national electrical code, local civil rights laws, political party state central committees, noxious weeds, nonresident deer hunting licenses, proprietary treatment systems, poultry associations, tax credits, alternative nicotine and vapor products, public assistance programs, judicial branch and county attorney salaries, civil litigation abuse, human trafficking, federal grants and loans notifications, quarterly payments to area education agencies, civic proficiency in higher education, charter schools under the Iowa public employees’ retirement system, school district incentives, extracurricular interscholastic eligibility, and levy increases, and including effective date, applicability, and retroactive applicability provisions.
ia:HF 2800.summary: As introduced, makes technical corrections related to laws enacted or considered in the 2026 session, including reorganizing the Code chapter on life insurance into subchapters.

ia:HF 2801.title: A bill for an act modifying the major economic growth attraction program, and including effective date provisions.
ia:HF 2801.summary: As introduced, changes the major economic growth attraction program to let the economic development authority award a tax credit of up to 10 percent of a qualifying investment in a rural county (population 50,000 or less), paid over 10 years.

ia:HF 523.title: A bill for an act relating to the ability of peace officers to file a petition for emergency protective orders on behalf of persons seeking relief from domestic abuse.
ia:HF 523.summary: As introduced, lets a peace officer file a petition for a 72-hour emergency protective order for a person who says they are in present danger of domestic abuse and asks the officer to file it.

ia:HF 571.title: A bill for an act relating to protections for medical practitioners and health care institutions, including those related to the exercise of conscience, whistleblower activities, and free speech, and providing penalties.
ia:HF 571.summary: As introduced, allows health care practitioners, institutions, and payors to refuse to take part in or pay for health care services that violate their conscience, and bars discrimination against them for refusing or for whistleblowing.

ia:HF 703.title: A bill for an act concerning information regarding certain state and federal student loan programs.
ia:HF 703.summary: As introduced, requires the Iowa student loan liquidity corporation to give the bureau of college aid estimated rates for federal Direct PLUS and state-offered loans, and sets related duties for the bureau and Iowa colleges.

ia:HF 766.title: A bill for an act relating to motor vehicle window tint, and making penalties applicable.
ia:HF 766.summary: As introduced, bars driving with front windshields under 70 percent light transmittance or side windows beside or ahead of the driver under 50 percent, replacing the state transportation department's rulemaking authority over window tint.

ia:HF 864.title: A bill for an act requiring persons who operate certain internet sites, applications, or a segment of an internet site or application that contains material pornographic for minors to perform reasonable age verification.
ia:HF 864.summary: As introduced, makes commercial entities that provide obscene material online liable if they do not use reasonable age verification, such as government ID or financial documents, for people accessing it.

ia:HF 960.title: A bill for an act relating to the sales tax exemption for the purchase of central office equipment or transmission equipment used by certain entities primarily in the furnishing of telecommunications services on a commercial basis.
ia:HF 960.summary: As introduced, expands the sales tax exemption for telecommunications central office and transmission equipment to all such equipment used in providing telecommunications services, removing the requirement that it be used primarily for that purpose.

ia:HF 990.title: A bill for an act relating to the issuance of medical cannabidiol registration cards and licensure of medical cannabidiol dispensaries.
ia:HF 990.summary: As introduced, raises the maximum number of licensed medical cannabidiol dispensaries in Iowa from 5 to 10 and removes the requirement to begin supplying by December 1, 2018.

ia:HF 992.title: A bill for an act relating to the fee for duplicates or other evidence of interstate fuel use tax permits or licenses.
ia:HF 992.summary: As introduced, raises the fee for a duplicate or other evidence of an interstate fuel permit or license from 50 cents to $1.

ia:SF 176.title: A bill for an act relating to participation in cocurricular and extracurricular activities offered by school districts by pupils who open enroll for purposes of receiving educational instruction and course content primarily over the internet.
ia:SF 176.summary: As introduced, lets students who open enroll in online instruction take part in their home district's extracurricular activities only if the online school's own attendance center does not sponsor those activities.

ia:SF 2039.title: A bill for an act providing for intervention by members of the general assembly in proceedings for judicial review of agency action under the Iowa administrative procedure Act. Effective date: 07/01/2026.
ia:SF 2039.summary: As introduced, allows the legislature's four top leaders to intervene in court reviews of state agency actions, and lets other legislators join their motion to intervene.

ia:SF 2187.title: A bill for an act relating to the verification of citizenship and immigration status of persons who apply for or renew a driver’s license or nonoperator’s identification card, and including applicability provisions.
ia:SF 2187.summary: As introduced, requires the Department of Transportation to check citizenship or lawful presence through a federal system for driver's license or ID applicants who do not prove citizenship, and bars issuing licenses if status cannot be verified.

ia:SF 2201.title: A bill for an act relating to school funding by establishing the state percent of growth and the categorical state percent of growth for the budget year beginning July 1, 2026, modifying provisions relating to property tax replacement payments, transportation equity aid funding, funding for school district budget adjustments, and school district enrollment, establishing an education support personnel salary supplement, making appropriations, and including effective date and applicability provisions.
ia:SF 2201.summary: As introduced, sets the state and categorical percent of growth for school funding at 1.75 percent for the budget year beginning July 1, 2026, and changes related school funding provisions.

ia:SF 2207.title: A bill for an act relating to the submission of proposed legislation by the governor and state departments and agencies.
ia:SF 2207.summary: As introduced, changes the deadline for state departments and agencies to submit proposed bills and joint resolutions to the Legislative Services Agency from 45 to 60 days before a session begins.

ia:SF 2218.title: A bill for an act relating to state regulatory compliance and eligibility requirements, including by modifying provisions related to the verification of the identity and employment eligibility of individuals by the board of educational examiners, school districts, accredited nonpublic schools, charter schools, and innovation zone schools; the provision of a false social security number to an employer, prospective employer, or a potential employee; qualifications for employment, professional licensure, voter registration, and bail; making penalties applicable; and including applicability provisions.
ia:SF 2218.summary: As introduced, requires the Board of Educational Examiners to require proof of lawful U.S. presence for teacher license applications and renewals, and sets identity and work eligibility verification duties for schools.

ia:SF 2219.title: A bill for an act requiring boards of directors of school districts, governing boards of charter schools, and authorities in charge of accredited nonpublic schools to adopt policies related to exempting student absences for school-sponsored activities, programs, competitions, and projects.
ia:SF 2219.summary: As introduced, requires school districts, charter schools, and accredited nonpublic schools to adopt policies giving students excused absences for 4-H or FFA activities.

ia:SF 2220.title: A bill for an act relating to education, including by modifying provisions related to the Iowa statewide assessment of student progress and programs for gifted and talented children, and by requiring school districts to develop an advanced mathematics pathway and implement procedures for subject acceleration and whole-grade acceleration, and including applicability provisions.
ia:SF 2220.summary: As introduced, changes education rules on the statewide student assessment and gifted programs, and requires school districts to create advanced math pathways and procedures for subject and whole-grade acceleration.

ia:SF 2263.title: A bill for an act relating to the carrying, transportation, and possession of weapons, and including effective date provisions.
ia:SF 2263.summary: As introduced, changes weapons laws, allowing dangerous weapons in a locked private vehicle in public nonsecure parking lots run by the state or local governments, along with other rules on carrying weapons.

ia:SF 2280.title: A bill for an act relating to the safety of persons in certain professions involved with the judicial system, including authorizing a member of the general assembly, judicial officer, attorney general, deputy attorney general, or assistant attorney general to be issued a professional permit to carry weapons, establishing the criminal offenses of threatening and the malicious sharing of personal information of a general assembly member or a judicial officer or a general assembly member’s or a judicial officer’s immediate family, and considering true threats to public officials as harassment, and providing penalties.
ia:SF 2280.summary: As introduced, allows legislators, judicial officers, and attorneys general to be issued professional weapons permits, and creates offenses for threatening judicial officers and maliciously sharing their or their families' personal information.

ia:SF 2284.title: A bill for an act relating to the use of automated systems that detect traffic violations or registration plate information, and making penalties applicable.
ia:SF 2284.summary: As introduced, bars sharing historical license plate reader location data with nongovernmental third parties when it could identify a person or vehicle, a simple misdemeanor, and bars citations from automated systems for brake or exhaust noise while a vehicle slows.

ia:SF 2299.title: A bill for an act relating to the district-to-community college sharing or concurrent enrollment program.
ia:SF 2299.summary: As introduced, requires parents, guardians, or students to repay a school the cost when a student fails a community college class taken through the concurrent enrollment program, if the school requests it.

ia:SF 2320.title: A bill for an act modifying provisions related to the district-to-community college sharing or concurrent enrollment program.
ia:SF 2320.summary: As introduced, requires students to take the in-person version of a community college course offered both in person and online, unless the school superintendent authorizes the online version.

ia:SF 2378.title: A bill for an act relating to the ability of property owners to protest proposed changes in zoning districts.
ia:SF 2378.summary: As introduced, repeals the right of property owners to file a written protest against a proposed change in a city zoning district.

ia:SF 2379.title: A bill for an act relating to victim protections including victim counselors, protective orders, sex offender registration, rights of sexual abuse victims, mental competency and civil commitment, restitution, and victim rights, and including effective date provisions.
ia:SF 2379.summary: As introduced, changes laws on crime victims, including confidentiality of victim counselors' communications, protective orders, sex offender registration, restitution, and victim rights.

ia:SF 2399.title: A bill for an act relating to bail and bond amounts and conditions.
ia:SF 2399.summary: As introduced, sets presumed minimum pretrial bond amounts for class A felonies ($500,000) and forcible class B, C, and D felonies ($25,000, $10,000, $5,000), and requires courts to weigh a defendant's danger to others.

ia:SF 2422.title: A bill for an act relating to public assistance programs under the purview of the department of health and human services, including the supplemental nutrition assistance program, Medicaid, and the Iowa health and wellness plan, and including effective date provisions.
ia:SF 2422.summary: As introduced, requires the state to verify citizenship or immigration status of public assistance applicants through a federal system, limits SNAP to eligible citizens and immigrants, and changes Medicaid managed care and other health and human services programs.

ia:SF 2426.title: A bill for an act relating to sufficient English language proficiency requirements for commercial drivers, providing penalties, and including applicability provisions.
ia:SF 2426.summary: As introduced, requires the Department of Transportation to test English proficiency of commercial driver's license and learner's permit applicants and renewals, and to deny those who cannot show the required reading and speaking ability.

ia:SF 2428.title: A bill for an act relating to education, including by modifying provisions related to the duties of the department of education; the discipline of students enrolled in school districts, charter schools, and innovation zone schools who cause violent or nonviolent disruptions; the responsibilities and powers of the department of education, school district teachers, and other educational staff related to students who have individualized education programs or plans under section 504 of the federal Rehabilitation Act; school district professional development plans; and authorizing teachers to request a meeting of a student’s individualized education program team.
ia:SF 2428.summary: As introduced, requires school districts and charter schools to adopt discipline policies for violent and nonviolent classroom disruptions, including teacher removal of a student for at least 30 minutes and an oversight committee deciding when the student returns.

ia:SF 2430.title: A bill for an act relating to the display of flags at half-staff on public buildings.
ia:SF 2430.summary: As introduced, requires custodians of public buildings to follow governor's proclamations on flying the U.S. and Iowa flags at half-staff, and lets the attorney general take legal action over violations.

ia:SF 2453.title: A bill for an act providing for investment by regents institutions in certified innovation funds and including effective date provisions.
ia:SF 2453.summary: As introduced, requires the University of Iowa, Iowa State, and University of Northern Iowa to invest at least 1 percent of their endowment assets by July 1, 2027, in innovation funds certified by the economic development authority.

ia:SF 2472.title: A bill for an act relating to state and local government taxes, fees, financial authority, and budgets, by modifying property assessment provisions, divisions of revenue, and funding from the secure an advanced vision for education fund, establishing a program for first-time homebuyers, modifying and making appropriations, and including effective date, applicability, and retroactive applicability provisions.
ia:SF 2472.summary: As introduced, changes state and local government tax and budget rules, including new limits on year-over-year growth in county and city property tax levy rates beginning with fiscal year 2027-2028.

ia:SF 2478.title: A bill for an act relating to transportation and other infrastructure-related appropriations to the department of transportation, including allocation and use of moneys from the road use tax fund and the primary road fund.
ia:SF 2478.summary: As introduced, appropriates money for fiscal year 2026-2027 from the road use tax fund and primary road fund to the Department of Transportation for operations, facilities, and related costs.

ia:SF 2484.title: A bill for an act relating to and making appropriations from the rebuild Iowa infrastructure fund, technology reinvestment fund, and renewable fuel infrastructure fund, providing for related matters including financial assistance eligibility for regional sports authority districts, department of health and human services information technology systems, the railway tracks overpass and underpass fund, and eligibility for entities to receive financial assistance from both the Iowa major events and tourism fund and the sports tourism infrastructure program, and including effective date provisions.
ia:SF 2484.summary: As introduced, appropriates money for fiscal year 2026-2027 from the Rebuild Iowa Infrastructure Fund and Technology Reinvestment Fund for state infrastructure and technology projects, and adjusts some earlier appropriations.

ia:SF 2488.title: A bill for an act relating to early childhood and family services, including the creation of an early childhood and family services system, making appropriations, convening an early childhood Iowa interim study committee, and including applicability, retroactive applicability, and effective date provisions.
ia:SF 2488.summary: As introduced, creates an early childhood and family services system under the Department of Health and Human Services, with districts delivering prevention and early intervention services for children under 19 and their families.

ia:SF 2490.title: A bill for an act relating to oil and gas production, including filing requirements, the authority of the department of natural resources, confidential information, pooling orders, negotiation of surface damage, imposition and distribution of a tax, and jurisdiction, and providing civil penalties.
ia:SF 2490.summary: As introduced, changes oil and gas rules, including yearly filings with the Department of Natural Resources, variances from its rules, five-year confidentiality of submitted information, pooling orders, surface damage negotiation, and a tax.

ia:SF 2493.title: A bill for an act relating to the excise tax on certain ethanol blended gasoline purchased exclusively for use in an implement of husbandry used in agricultural production.
ia:SF 2493.summary: As introduced, exempts gasoline with more than 85 percent ethanol from the state fuel excise tax when bought at a terminal for use in agricultural implements, with buyers supporting the purchase using a revenue department exemption certificate.

ia:SF 273.title: A bill for an act relating to mandatory reporting to the board of educational examiners of licensed school employees who engage in grooming behavior toward students.
ia:SF 273.summary: As introduced, redefines "grooming behavior" that schools must report to the board of educational examiners as a pattern of behavior to entice or entrap a student in order to take advantage of the student, including through a sex act.

ia:SF 274.title: A bill for an act relating to forms of payment for entry into an extracurricular interscholastic athletic contest or competition.
ia:SF 274.summary: As introduced, requires public schools and athletic organizations registered with the Department of Education to accept legal tender as payment for entry to interscholastic athletic events.

ia:SF 304.title: A bill for an act providing an exception to a minor’s legal capacity to consent to the provision of medical care or services for a sexually transmitted disease or infection.
ia:SF 304.summary: As introduced, removes a minor's legal ability to consent to vaccinations for sexually transmitted diseases or infections, while leaving consent to prevention, diagnosis and treatment otherwise unchanged.

ia:SF 378.title: A bill for an act relating to speed limits, including the speed limit range for which certain excessive speed violations cannot be considered for certain purposes and the default speed limit for all vehicular traffic, and making penalties applicable.
ia:SF 378.summary: As introduced, raises the default speed limit for roads where no other limit applies from 55 to 60 miles per hour.

ia:SF 469.title: A bill for an act creating an emeritus license to practice medicine and surgery or osteopathic medicine and surgery.
ia:SF 469.summary: As introduced, requires the Board of Medicine to issue three-year emeritus licenses to physicians aged 60 or older who mainly supervise and train resident physicians, keeping their scope of practice without continuing education requirements.

ia:SF 473.title: A bill for an act relating to certain sincerely held religious or moral beliefs of certain entities for purposes of child foster care and adoption.
ia:SF 473.summary: As introduced, bars the Department of Health and Human Services from requiring foster parents to affirm policies on sexual orientation or gender identity that conflict with their religious or moral beliefs, or denying licenses based on those beliefs.

ia:SF 563.title: A bill for an act relating to the licensure of crematory operators and funeral establishments, and making penalties applicable.
ia:SF 563.summary: As introduced, requires the Board of Mortuary Science to license crematory operators, including a specialized cremation course, and grants a license to funeral directors who apply.

ia:SF 654.title: A bill for an act relating to wildlife, including the treatment of beaver dams, identification for traps, snares, and tree stands, maximum fur dealer license fees, and deer depredation, and making penalties applicable.
ia:SF 654.summary: As introduced, changes wildlife rules, including requiring identification plates on deer stands placed on public land, with a $30 fine for violations, and addressing beaver dams, trap identification, and fur dealer license fees.

ia:SF 93.title: A bill for an act relating to qualifications to serve as a commissioner or an executive director for a county commission of veteran affairs. Effective date: 07/01/2026.
ia:SF 93.summary: As introduced, allows current or former Iowa National Guard and Iowa-based reserve members with honorable or satisfactory service, not only veterans, to serve on county veterans affairs commissions.

id:H 508.title: TRANSPORTATION – Amends and adds to existing law to revise provisions regarding bicycle and pedestrian projects.
id:H 508.summary: As introduced, revises a definition in Idaho transportation code, allows federal funds and grants to be used to improve bicycle and pedestrian facilities, and amends a provision on violations.

id:H 522.title: UNMANNED AIRCRAFT SYSTEMS – Adds to existing law to establish provisions regarding unmanned aircraft systems near Department of Correction facilities.
id:H 522.summary: As introduced, makes it a misdemeanor, with a $2,000 to $5,000 fine or up to a year in jail, to operate a drone in restricted airspace over a correctional facility, and lets corrections or law enforcement officers take reasonable measures against drones operating nearby.

id:H 542.title: SOCIAL MEDIA – Adds to existing law to establish the Stop Harms from Addictive Social Media Act.
id:H 542.summary: As introduced, requires covered social media platforms to get parental consent for accounts of users age 16 and under and to refrain from addictive interface design features for those users.

id:H 561.title: STATE GOVERNMENT AND STATE AFFAIRS – Amends existing law to revise and remove provisions regarding flags flown by a governmental entity, to provide a penalty, and to establish provisions regarding enforcement by the Attorney General.
id:H 561.summary: As introduced, sets a civil penalty of $2,000 per flag per day for government entities that fly flags in violation of state law, enforced by the Attorney General through civil actions in district court.

id:H 602.title: FOREIGN LAWS – Adds to existing law to establish provisions prohibiting the use of foreign laws in Idaho courts.
id:H 602.summary: As introduced, bars the use of foreign laws and foreign legal doctrines in Idaho courts.

id:H 650.title: STATE GOVERNMENT AND STATE AFFAIRS – Adds to existing law to provide for state sovereignty, jurisdictional presumption, and a limitation on federal power.
id:H 650.summary: As introduced, declares a strong presumption that Idaho has jurisdiction over matters within the state unless the U.S. Constitution clearly and specifically grants authority to the federal government.

id:H 667.title: MOTOR VEHICLES – Amends existing law to eliminate the nondomiciled CDL program in Idaho.
id:H 667.summary: As introduced, bars Idaho from honoring learner's permits from other states or countries for commercial driver's licenses, which will be issued only to those who complete the entire process in Idaho.

id:H 674.title: TELECOMMUNICATION SERVICE – Amends and adds to existing law to revise provisions regarding the discontinuation of telecommunication service.
id:H 674.summary: As introduced, clarifies when the Public Utilities Commission recognizes and relies on Federal Communications Commission authorization for a provider to withdraw telephone service.

id:H 750.title: TRANSACTIONS – Amends and adds to existing law to establish provisions regarding programmable money.
id:H 750.summary: As introduced, excludes "programmable money" from the Uniform Commercial Code definition of money, limits issuers' ability to restrict or deny transactions based on lawful personal characteristics or activities, bars social credit scoring through it, and sets civil and criminal penalties.

id:H 752.title: INDECENCY AND OBSCENITY – Adds to existing law to prohibit a person from entering a restroom or changing room of the opposite sex, to provide a penalty, and to provide exceptions.
id:H 752.summary: As introduced, makes it a misdemeanor to knowingly enter a restroom, changing room, locker room or shower room in a government building or public accommodation designated for the opposite biological sex; a repeat conviction within five years is a felony, with exceptions.

id:H 758.title: DAYCARE LICENSING – Amends existing law to provide for supervision requirements while a child is sleeping and to establish an exception regarding children to be counted in attendance at a daycare.
id:H 758.summary: As introduced, lets in-home day care providers use a video device to monitor a sleeping child and exempts providers' own school-age children from the headcount used for licensing.

id:H 766.title: DEVELOPMENT IMPACT FEES – Amends existing law to revise a definition regarding which governmental entities are authorized to adopt development impact fees.
id:H 766.summary: As introduced, adds fire and ambulance service districts to the entities that may adopt development impact fee ordinances, alongside cities, counties and single county-wide highway districts.

id:H 788.title: MEDICAID – Adds to existing law to establish provisions regarding Medicaid prior authorization exemptions for certain preceptorships.
id:H 788.summary: As introduced, gives primary care, psychiatry and obstetrics physicians who provide at least 360 hours of qualifying teaching preceptorship, 60 percent in rural areas, a 12-month exemption from Medicaid prior authorization, capped at 100 physicians per specialty annually.

id:H 810.title: ELECTIONS – Amends existing law to provide certain physical presence requirements for state representatives and senators.
id:H 810.summary: As introduced, requires legislative candidates to be registered electors for one year and to live in their declared primary residence in the district at least 120 days before filing, with exemptions for military service or a religious mission.

id:H 822.title: PEDIATRIC SECRETIVE TRANSITIONS PARENTAL RIGHTS ACT – Adds to existing law to establish the Pediatric Secretive Transitions Parental Rights Act.
id:H 822.summary: As introduced, bars health providers, schools and child care providers from facilitating a minor's medical or social transition without parental consent, requires schools to notify parents within 72 hours of name, pronoun or facility requests, and lets parents sue.

id:H 849.title: EDUCATION – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding certain placement and movement on the career ladder.
id:H 849.summary: As introduced, lets career and technical education teachers and qualified school service professionals, such as counselors and nurses, who enter K-12 from private industry advance a Career Ladder rung after one proficient evaluation year instead of four.

id:H 855.title: FISH AND GAME – Amends existing law regarding lifetime hunting and fishing licenses.
id:H 855.summary: As introduced, requires five years of Idaho residency, instead of six months, to buy a lifetime hunting or fishing license.

id:H 863.title: MEDICAID – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding provider payment.
id:H 863.summary: As introduced, reduces Medicaid payment rates for residential habilitation providers, cutting General Fund Medicaid spending by $21.8 million in fiscal 2027, and requires the department to report to the Legislature how those funds are used.

id:H 879.title: INDUSTRIAL HEMP – Amends existing law to provide for the sale of hemp products intended for human ingestion or inhalation.
id:H 879.summary: As introduced, makes establishments that sell certain hemp products at retail subject to the existing Industrial Hemp Research and Development Act.

id:H 889.title: STATE PROCUREMENT – Amends, repeals, and adds to existing law regarding the procurement of property by the State of Idaho.
id:H 889.summary: As introduced, revises state procurement rules by defining new terms, setting best-and-final offer procedures, allowing multiple-award contracts, requiring bid scoring to be published with solicitations, and letting prior state contract performance count toward bid qualification.

id:H 895.title: DATA CENTERS – Adds to existing law to establish limitations on consumptive use of water for cooling certain data centers.
id:H 895.summary: As introduced, requires new data centers to cool without consuming water, or to use water from a municipal, water district, or water and sewer district system.

id:H 898.title: STATE HISTORIC PRESERVATION OFFICER – Amends, repeals, and adds to existing law to provide for the State Historic Preservation Officer.
id:H 898.summary: As introduced, moves the State Historic Preservation Office from the Idaho State Historical Society to the new Office of Species, Minerals, and Energy Coordination in the Governor's office.

id:H 911.title: PUBLIC UTILITIES – Adds to existing law to provide for new large loads.
id:H 911.summary: As introduced, requires new large electrical loads to receive utility service only under a Public Utilities Commission-approved contract filed before service begins and supported by a "no harm test" for existing ratepayers.

id:H 913.title: MEDICAID – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding Medicaid eligibility expansion.
id:H 913.summary: As introduced, requires the Department of Health and Welfare to implement Medicaid work and community engagement requirements by December 31, 2026, verifying compliance for the three months before enrollment or redetermination.

id:H 919.title: APPROPRIATIONS – DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATION – PERMANENT BUILDING FUND – Relates to the appropriation to the Department of Administration for the Division of Public Works for fiscal year 2027.
id:H 919.summary: As introduced, appropriates $72.5 million from the Permanent Building Fund for fiscal 2027 state building maintenance, alteration and repair, ADA projects and Capitol Mall and Chinden Campus facilities, plus design of a Bonneville County readiness center.

id:H 923.title: APPROPRIATIONS – DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATION – Relates to the appropriation to the Department of Administration for fiscal year 2027.
id:H 923.summary: As introduced, appropriates an additional $782,000 for fiscal 2027 to the Department of Administration, shifting utilities costs to dedicated funds and funding a Medicaid procurement bureau chief, utilities increases and IT hardware.

id:H 924.title: APPROPRIATIONS – STATE LIQUOR DIVISION – Relates to the appropriation to the State Liquor Division for fiscal year 2027.
id:H 924.summary: As introduced, appropriates fiscal 2027 funding increases to the State Liquor Division for utilities and supplies inflation, replacing store security systems, shelving and equipment, and IT and security equipment.

id:H 928.title: MERIT-BASED HEALTH CARE – Adds to existing law to establish the Merit-Based Health Care Act.
id:H 928.summary: As introduced, requires Medicaid-funded hiring and contracting decisions to be based solely on merit and qualifications, bars specified diversity practices such as race- or sex-based preferences, and enforces it through Attorney General civil penalties.

id:H 929.title: HEALTH CARE – Adds to existing law to establish provisions regarding certain out-of-pocket payments for health care services.
id:H 929.summary: As introduced, bars health insurers from preventing providers from offering discounted cash prices, lets patients' cash payments count toward deductibles and out-of-pocket maximums with documentation, and requires providers to accept cash payments as full settlement. Effective July 1, 2026.

id:H 930.title: CAMPAIGN FINANCE – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding the duties of political treasurers.
id:H 930.summary: As introduced, requires candidates and political committees to keep campaign money in a separate checking account, requires reporting personal loans over $1,000, and limits investing campaign funds to cash-equivalent accounts, not stocks.

id:H 934.title: TAXATION – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding the Idaho Parental Choice Tax Credit.
id:H 934.summary: As introduced, makes technical corrections to the Idaho Parental Choice Tax Credit: eligible students are ages 5 to 18 at any time in the tax year, tutoring must be academic, and advance payments may be claimed only initially.

id:H 939.title: HUNTING – Amends existing law regarding the use of certain technologies.
id:H 939.summary: As introduced, regulates the use of thermal imaging, night vision, transmitting trail cameras and drones for hunting, with exemptions including for predators and for agricultural purposes.

id:H 940.title: EDUCATION – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding the Idaho Digital Learning Academy.
id:H 940.summary: As introduced, limits the Idaho Digital Learning Alliance to supplemental online courses focused on grades 6-12, ends offerings such as virtual school participation and K-5 programs, sets minimum course fees, and caps state funding at $445 per course.

id:H 942.title: APPROPRIATIONS – MILLENNIUM INCOME FUND – Relates to the appropriation from the Idaho Millennium Income Fund for fiscal year 2027.
id:H 942.summary: As introduced, appropriates the Idaho Millennium Income Fund tobacco settlement money for fiscal 2027 to behavioral health and youth programs, including Kamiah Recovery Center and the Idaho Children's Trust Fund.

id:H 964.title: APPROPRIATIONS – DEPARTMENT OF FISH AND GAME – Relates to the appropriation to the Department of Fish and Game for fiscal year 2027.
id:H 964.summary: As introduced, appropriates an additional $14.2 million for fiscal 2027 to the Department of Fish and Game for fisheries habitat, wolf depredation response and other items, and directs use of funds for wolf trapping.

id:H 966.title: APPROPRIATIONS – DEPARTMENT OF CORRECTION – Relates to the appropriation to the Department of Correction for fiscal year 2027.
id:H 966.summary: As introduced, appropriates $200,000 a year from the General Fund to the Department of Correction to cover House Bill 684, which lets sheriffs seek reimbursement for retrieving absconders from out of state.

id:H 971.title: APPROPRIATIONS – OFFICE OF THE ATTORNEY GENERAL – Relates to the appropriation to the Office of the Attorney General for fiscal years 2026 and 2027.
id:H 971.summary: As introduced, appropriates $880,000 in each of fiscal 2026 and 2027 to the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Fund and allows the money to be used for any of the Attorney General's duties, not only consumer protection.

id:H 972.title: APPROPRIATIONS – HEALTH AND WELFARE – DIVISION OF WELFARE – Relates to the appropriation to the Department of Health and Welfare for fiscal year 2027.
