id:H 972.summary: As introduced, appropriates $351,000 from the General Fund and $163,000 in federal funds for fiscal 2027 to the Division of Welfare for system changes needed to carry out House Bill 730 on SNAP eligibility.

id:H 973.title: APPROPRIATIONS – MILITARY DIVISION – Relates to the appropriation to the Military Division for fiscal year 2026.
id:H 973.summary: As introduced, appropriates $6.5 million in federal funds for fiscal 2026 to the Military Division to replace climate control systems in Idaho Air National Guard buildings at Gowen Field.

id:H 975.title: APPROPRIATIONS – Relates to the appropriation and transfer of moneys in the state treasury for fiscal year 2027.
id:H 975.summary: As introduced, directs that no Budget Stabilization Fund transfer occur even if the fund balance exceeds 15 percent of General Fund revenues, leaving the $880.2 million balance unchanged in fiscal 2027.

id:H 978.title: APPROPRIATIONS – HEALTH AND WELFARE – PUBLIC HEALTH SERVICES – Relates to the appropriation to the Department of Health and Welfare for fiscal year 2027.
id:H 978.summary: As introduced, adds $35.1 million to the Health and Welfare Department's Public Health Services budget for fiscal 2027, including restoring the Immunization Assessment Fund, and moves the Idaho Home Visiting Program to another division.

id:HJM 19.title: EDUCATION – States findings of the Legislature, supports federal efforts to eliminate the U.S. Department of Education, and urges Congress to fully cooperate with these efforts.
id:HJM 19.summary: As introduced, states the Idaho Legislature's support for eliminating the U.S. Department of Education and returning primary authority over education policy to the states. It does not change funding.

id:S 1247.title: MEMORANDUM OF AGREEMENT – Adds to existing law to establish provisions regarding law enforcement entering into a memorandum of agreement.
id:S 1247.summary: As introduced, creates the Idaho E-Verify Act, requiring state and local agencies, and private employers with 150 or more employees and government contracts of $100,000 or more, to use the federal E-Verify program for new hires.

id:S 1288.title: EDUCATION – Adds to existing law to provide for the establishment of the Idaho High-Needs Student Fund.
id:S 1288.summary: As introduced, creates the Idaho High Needs Student Fund to reimburse school districts and charter schools, through an application to the Department of Education, for extraordinary costs of serving students with disabilities. The governor recommended $5 million.

id:S 1294.title: INFANTS AND NEWBORNS – Adds to existing law to establish provisions regarding hearing loss screening.
id:S 1294.summary: As introduced, establishes a program to screen newborns for hearing loss at birth, funded only with federal money.

id:S 1297.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE – Adds to existing law to establish the Conversational AI Safety Act.
id:S 1297.summary: As introduced, sets safety standards for conversational AI services, requiring operators to adopt response protocols, show a persistent AI disclaimer to known minors, prevent sexually explicit content, bar engagement-driving "gamification", and offer parental supervision tools.

id:S 1300.title: STATE GOVERNMENT – Amends current law to revise provisions regarding director appointments to certain executive agencies.
id:S 1300.summary: As introduced, makes the directors of the Transportation, Fish and Game, and Parks and Recreation departments gubernatorial appointees subject to Senate confirmation.

id:S 1336.title: EDUCATION – Amends and adds to existing law to revise and establish provisions regarding civics education.
id:S 1336.summary: As introduced, sets civics curriculum requirements for public schools and charters: two credits each in American history and government for secondary students, Western Civilization in 8th grade by 2030-31, and instruction on the American Founding and the history of Communism.

id:S 1352.title: HOUSING – Adds to existing law to establish provisions regarding starter home subdivisions.
id:S 1352.summary: As introduced, allows small-lot starter home subdivisions on residential land, setting state standards for lot size, frontage, setbacks and density and overriding local zoning that prevents them.

id:S 1354.title: ACCESSORY DWELLING UNITS – Amends and adds to existing law to revise provisions regarding prohibitions against restrictive covenants banning accessory dwelling units and to establish provisions regarding accessory dwelling units in the Local Land Use Planning Act.
id:S 1354.summary: As introduced, treats accessory dwelling units as a residential use allowed by right in cities when conditions are met, with objective approval standards, and bars cities from banning or unreasonably restricting them.

id:S 1401.title: APPROPRIATIONS – HEALTH AND WELFARE – PUBLIC HEALTH SERVICES – Relates to the appropriation to the Department of Health and Welfare for fiscal year 2027.
id:S 1401.summary: As introduced, appropriates an additional $35.6 million for fiscal 2027 to Public Health Services, including restoring the Immunization Assessment Fund, and moves the Idaho Home Visiting Program to the early learning division.

id:S 1404.title: APPROPRIATIONS – DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE – Relates to the appropriation to the Department of Agriculture for fiscal years 2026 and 2027.
id:S 1404.summary: As introduced, appropriates an additional $829,900 for fiscal 2027 to the Department of Agriculture for IT hardware, vehicles, lab and field equipment and boat inspection signs, plus fiscal 2026 funds for exotic pest control and quagga mussel treatment.

id:S 1405.title: APPROPRIATIONS – SOIL AND WATER CONSERVATION COMMISSION – Relates to the appropriation to the Soil and Water Conservation Commission for fiscal years 2026 and 2027.
id:S 1405.summary: As introduced, appropriates fiscal 2027 funding for the Soil and Water Conservation Commission, including Conservation Reserve Enhancement Program payments, and moves the commission from the Department of Agriculture to the Department of Water Resources.

id:S 1408.title: APPROPRIATIONS – PUBLIC SCHOOLS – EDUCATIONAL SERVICES FOR THE DEAF AND THE BLIND – Relates to the appropriation to the Public Schools Educational Support Program’s Division of Educational Services for the Deaf and the Blind for fiscal year 2027.
id:S 1408.summary: As introduced, appropriates an additional $356,300 for fiscal 2027 to the Idaho Educational Services for the Deaf and the Blind, including pay parity with the career ladder and replacement of a bus and van.

id:S 1409.title: APPROPRIATIONS – IDAHO STATE POLICE – Relates to the appropriation to the Idaho State Police for fiscal year 2027.
id:S 1409.summary: As introduced, appropriates an additional $4.9 million for fiscal 2027 to the Idaho State Police for a commercial vehicle safety grant, a mobile Livescan program and replacement patrol vehicles and equipment.

id:S 1416.title: APPROPRIATIONS – SMEC – Relates to the appropriation to the Office of Species, Minerals, and Energy Coordination for fiscal year 2027.
id:S 1416.summary: As introduced, appropriates $46.1 million for fiscal 2027 to the new Office of Species, Minerals, and Energy Coordination, which merges the energy and mineral resources and species conservation offices, plus added funding for nuclear projects, fish habitat and energy resiliency grants.

id:S 1417.title: APPROPRIATIONS – DEPARTMENT OF PARKS AND RECREATION – Relates to the appropriation to the Department of Parks and Recreation for fiscal years 2027 and 2026.
id:S 1417.summary: As introduced, appropriates fiscal 2027 funding increases to the Department of Parks and Recreation, including staff and operations for a new park near Salmon, trail maintenance, RV campsites and a roundabout at Farragut State Park.

id:S 1418.title: KRATOM – Adds to existing law to establish the Idaho Kratom Consumer Protection and Safety Act.
id:S 1418.summary: As introduced, creates the Idaho Kratom Consumer Protection and Safety Act, which bans making or selling kratom products with artificially elevated 7-hydroxymitragynine, sets age restrictions and gives enforcement authority with civil penalties.

id:S 1424.title: MOTOR VEHICLES – Amends existing law to provide for an exception for licensed dealers in Idaho for a manufacturer or distributor with a manufacturer-owned or distributor-owned dealership.
id:S 1424.summary: As introduced, prohibits vehicle manufacturers that had not begun doing so before January 1, 2026 from selling vehicles directly to consumers without using franchised dealers, and updates Idaho's dealer franchise laws.

id:S 1426.title: IDAHO TRANSPORTATION DEPARTMENT – FUNDING – Relates to the funding of the Idaho Transportation Department for fiscal year 2027.
id:S 1426.summary: As introduced, appropriates an additional $98.9 million for fiscal 2027 to the Idaho Transportation Department for deferred maintenance, equipment, airfields and construction and right-of-way acquisition.

id:S 1427.title: APPROPRIATIONS – DEPARTMENT OF LANDS – Relates to the appropriation to the Department of Lands for fiscal years 2026 and 2027.
id:S 1427.summary: As introduced, appropriates fiscal 2027 enhancements to the Department of Lands, including fire radio equipment, a vehicle storage structure, vehicles, computer hardware, and partial restoration of fire preparedness funding.

id:S 1430.title: FIREARMS – Amends existing law to revise a provision regarding preemption of firearms regulation, to provide a penalty, and to provide for a cause of action.
id:S 1430.summary: As introduced, sets a civil penalty and permanent injunction for local governments that knowingly violate state firearms laws, with the Attorney General giving 30 days' notice to cure before court action.

id:S 1431.title: APPROPRIATIONS – DEPARTMENT OF WATER RESOURCES – Relates to the appropriation to the Department of Water Resources for fiscal year 2027.
id:S 1431.summary: As introduced, appropriates an additional $390,000 onetime for fiscal 2027 to the Department of Water Resources for aquifer monitoring, stream gaging and adjudication staff.

id:S 1433.title: APPROPRIATIONS – HEALTH AND WELFARE – MEDICAID – Relates to the appropriation to the Department of Health and Welfare for fiscal years 2026 and 2027.
id:S 1433.summary: As introduced, appropriates an additional $493.4 million for fiscal 2027 to the Division of Medicaid, including funding for the claims system procurement, estate recovery, program integrity and Hospital Assessment Fund adjustments.

id:S 1435.title: APPROPRIATIONS – HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES – Relates to the maintenance appropriations to the Department of Health and Welfare and the State Independent Living Council for fiscal year 2027.
id:S 1435.summary: As introduced, sets the fiscal 2027 maintenance budget for the Department of Health and Welfare and State Independent Living Council, with standard cost adjustments, a base reduction of up to 5 percent, and the cost of House Bill 863.

id:S 1436.title: STATE PROCUREMENT – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding cooperative and group discount purchasing.
id:S 1436.summary: As introduced, clarifies that shared, group discount and cooperative purchasing contracts may include state-specific modifications to the underlying contract.

id:S 1444.title: APPROPRIATIONS – PUBLIC SCHOOLS – DIVISION OF STUDENT SUPPORT – Relates to the appropriation to the Public Schools Educational Support Program’s Division of Student Support for fiscal years 2026 and 2027.
id:S 1444.summary: As introduced, appropriates an additional $2.2 million ongoing for public school student support, adds federal grant spending authority, and reduces discretionary funding for virtual-only schools.

id:S 1446.title: APPROPRIATIONS – Relates to the appropriation to the Department of Health and Welfare and the Judicial Branch for fiscal year 2027.
id:S 1446.summary: As introduced, restores Assertive Community Treatment and peer support services using internal savings, Millennium Income Fund and opioid settlement money, appropriating about $30.7 million for fiscal 2027.

id:S 1447.title: APPROPRIATIONS – PUBLIC SCHOOLS – STUDENT SUPPORT DIVISION – Relates to the appropriation to the Public Schools Educational Support Program’s Division of Student Support for fiscal year 2027.
id:S 1447.summary: As introduced, appropriates $5 million for fiscal 2027 from the Idaho High Needs Student Fund for school districts and charter schools, and transfers $5 million into that fund from other accounts.

id:S 1448.title: MINORS – Amends existing law to revise provisions regarding material harmful to minors.
id:S 1448.summary: As introduced, adds definitions and clarifying language to Idaho's 2024 Children's and Library Protection Act, responding to a Ninth Circuit opinion and a U.S. Supreme Court decision on Texas's age-verification law.

id:S 1452.title: APPROPRIATIONS – PUBLIC SCHOOLS – IDAHO DIGITAL LEARNING ACADEMY – Relates to the appropriation to the Public Schools Educational Support Program’s Division of the Idaho Digital Learning Academy for fiscal year 2027.
id:S 1452.summary: As introduced, changes the public school budget bill so Idaho Digital Learning Academy course fees are not all capped at $40, allowing a $100 minimum fee for non-graduation courses as House Bill 940 provides.

id:S 1454.title: APPROPRIATIONS – HEALTH AND WELFARE – EARLY LEARNING AND DEVELOPMENT, YOUTH SAFETY AND PERMANENCY, AND FAMILY AND COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIPS – Relates to the appropriation to the Department of Health and Welfare for fiscal years 2026 and 2027.
id:S 1454.summary: As introduced, appropriates an additional $5.7 million for fiscal 2027 to Health and Welfare divisions for early learning, family partnerships and youth safety, and adds the Idaho Home Visiting Program to the early learning division.

il:HB 2955.title: EPA-PFAS WASTEWATER
il:HB 2955.summary: As introduced, creates a PFAS Wastewater Citizen Protection Committee to deliver a PFAS Action Plan within a year, update it annually and report, with technical help from the Illinois Sustainable Technology Center. The Act is repealed December 31, 2044.

il:HB 3275.title: SCH-CARDIAC EMERGENCY RESPONSE
il:HB 3275.summary: As introduced, requires interscholastic athletic associations to require school coaches to hold CPR, first aid and AED certification, and requires school cardiac emergency response plans to include a certified response team and annual drills.

il:HB 3711.title: PROFESSIONAL MISCONDUCT
il:HB 3711.summary: As introduced, requires health professionals and institutions to report specified sexual and violent misconduct to the state professional regulation department, requires law enforcement and prosecutors to report charges and convictions of licensees, and creates a Sexual Assault Survivors Fund.

il:SB 3107.title: QUICK-TAKE OAK PARK
il:SB 3107.summary: As introduced, allows the Village of Oak Park to use quick-take eminent domain for two years to acquire specified properties on Madison Street and Humphrey Avenue in Cook County for a public building and facility.

in:HB 1001.title: Housing matters.
in:HB 1001.summary: Changes housing rules by limiting fees units of government may charge for building permits after 2026, requiring annual housing status reports from local governments, and revising loan allocations from the residential housing infrastructure fund.

in:HB 1002.title: Electric utility affordability.
in:HB 1002.summary: Requires electric utilities to put households applying for energy assistance on levelized billing with opt-outs, bars residential shutoffs when the forecast heat index is 95 or higher, and requires investor-owned utilities to seek rate changes through three-year rate plans.

in:HB 1003.title: Boards and commissions.
in:HB 1003.summary: Creates an agricultural promotion and regulation task force, repeals the fire prevention and building safety commission and moves its duties to the homeland security department, and repeals, merges or changes various other state boards and commissions.

in:HB 1004.title: Various education matters.
in:HB 1004.summary: Changes many state education laws, including removing spending restrictions for remediation programs, allowing temporary contracts for teachers on emergency permits, and moving firearm safety educational materials duties from the Department of Education to the Department of Homeland Security.

in:HB 1038.title: Gaming matters.
in:HB 1038.summary: Requires Allen, DeKalb and Steuben counties to put an inland casino question on the 2026 ballot, lets the gaming commission award a casino license there if voters approve, and limits horse racing satellite facility licenses to three.

in:HB 1042.title: Regulation and investment of cryptocurrency.
in:HB 1042.summary: Requires state retirement and savings plans to offer a self-directed brokerage account with a cryptocurrency option, and bars state and local bodies from restricting or taxing the use of digital assets as payment.

in:HB 1052.title: Various administrative law matters.
in:HB 1052.summary: Adds grounds for the horse racing commission to revoke licenses, sets civil penalties for sweepstakes games, adds sports wagering to the voluntary exclusion program, and changes beer wholesaler and wine retailer permit rules.

in:HB 1056.title: Resisting law enforcement conflict resolution.
in:HB 1056.summary: Resolves a conflict between two 2025 laws, HEA 1014 and HEA 1637, concerning resisting law enforcement.

in:HB 1062.title: Wake boarding and wake surfing.
in:HB 1062.summary: Sets restrictions, with a penalty, on wake boarding and wake surfing on public freshwater lakes, and separate restrictions on small lakes.

in:HB 1065.title: Ban on gratuities for public officials.
in:HB 1065.summary: Makes it a Class A misdemeanor to commingle campaign committee funds with the personal funds of a committee officer, member or associate, and a Level 6 felony if $50,000 or more is commingled.

in:HB 1088.title: Technical corrections.
in:HB 1088.summary: Fixes spelling, formatting, grammar and cross-reference issues in the Indiana Code and resolves technical conflicts from the 2025 session.

in:HB 1098.title: Work based learning liability.
in:HB 1098.summary: Requires intermediaries and employers in work based learning programs to sign a duties agreement, and makes participating students eligible for workers' compensation benefits, subject to limits.

in:HB 1114.title: Coverage for certain cancer prescriptions.
in:HB 1114.summary: Bars state employee plans, insurers and HMOs that cover advanced metastatic cancer from requiring patients to fail on, or have a history of failing, a different drug before covering a prescription.

in:HB 1115.title: Homeowners association governance.
in:HB 1115.summary: Requires homeowners association boards to give members four days' written notice of board meetings with an agenda, counts remote attendees as present at member meetings, requires a fine schedule before fines, and limits consent needed to amend governing documents to two-thirds of owners.

in:HB 1116.title: Virtual currency kiosks.
in:HB 1116.summary: Bans the operation of virtual currency kiosks in Indiana, makes violations actionable by the attorney general as deceptive consumer sales, and allows forfeiture of kiosk charges and the kiosks themselves for knowing violations.

in:HB 1122.title: License plates for former state legislators.
in:HB 1122.summary: Allows special license plates for former legislators who served at least five House terms, at least three Senate terms, or 12 combined years in both chambers.

in:HB 1131.title: Licensed estheticians and electrologists.
in:HB 1131.summary: Expands the definition of esthetician to cover microneedling with proof of advanced training on request, and lets electrologist applicants skip cosmetology or esthetician licensure while meeting a combined 600 hours of education and experience.

in:HB 1145.title: Thirteenth check.
in:HB 1145.summary: Lets members of the excise police and conservation officers' retirement plan choose a joint and survivor payout, and provides a thirteenth retirement check in 2026 to certain members of several state retirement funds.

in:HB 1147.title: Licensure of certified public accountants.
in:HB 1147.summary: Makes a bachelor's degree with an accounting concentration, or equivalent as the board decides, enough to be eligible to take the CPA licensure exam.

in:HB 1150.title: Local regulation.
in:HB 1150.summary: Bars homeowners association rules that restrict vehicles or outdoor equipment by fuel type or prohibit displaying an American flag, and bars associations from installing or allowing automated license plate readers unless installed by law enforcement.

in:HB 1152.title: Homeowners association matters.
in:HB 1152.summary: Lets homeowners associations raise budgets without a quorum within set limits (110% in the first five years after first sale, then the lesser of 105% or Midwest housing price inflation), bars charging fees for services, and bars banning amateur radio antennas.

in:HB 1155.title: Traffic enforcement.
in:HB 1155.summary: Creates a pilot project letting large homeowners association subdivisions (1,500+ lots, 15+ miles of private road) set speed limits and stop signs that police can enforce on their private roads.

in:HB 1161.title: Local government matters.
in:HB 1161.summary: Makes certain county board appointees serve at the pleasure of the appointing authority, staggers terms on nine-member local health boards, and changes oath-of-office procedures for town police commissioners in reorganized subdivisions.

in:HB 1165.title: Various animal related matters.
in:HB 1165.summary: Increases penalties for certain animal offenses, changes animal offense definitions, applies animal cruelty law to rodents that are not nuisances, and removes partial liability for people who remove an animal from a vehicle.

in:HB 1177.title: Child care assistance.
in:HB 1177.summary: Raises the maximum employer size eligible for the employer child care expenditure income tax credit, and counts child care facility operating costs and contracted child care services for employees as qualified expenses.

in:HB 1192.title: Seed laws.
in:HB 1192.summary: Writes various administrative rules into the Indiana seed law, repeals certain administrative rules, and makes conforming and technical changes.

in:HB 1193.title: Civil rights commission.
in:HB 1193.summary: Bars the civil rights commission from representing private individuals in court, requires it to refer complaints first to other agencies with jurisdiction, and limits it to representing the state in civil actions.

in:HB 1200.title: Bureau of motor vehicles.
in:HB 1200.summary: Changes motor vehicle and driver licensing law, including barring INDOT from using variable speed limits, setting the driver's license age at 16 instead of 16 years 90 days, and requiring English proficiency for commercial motor vehicle operators.

in:HB 1202.title: Various public safety matters.
in:HB 1202.summary: Requires ignition interlock vendors to register devices with the toxicology department, limits interlock use to alcohol-related OWI offenses, and requires homeland security department inspections before child care centers, ministries and child caring institutions are licensed.

in:HB 1249.title: Various criminal law matters.
in:HB 1249.summary: Sets minimum jail time or community service for drunk driving with one or two prior convictions (10 or 20 days) with good time credit, treats watercraft as vehicles for OWI, and adds drug-impaired OWI to habitual traffic violator law.

in:HB 1254.title: Various dental matters; respiratory care.
in:HB 1254.summary: Changes education requirements for dental hygienists, nitrous oxide rules for hygienists, requirements for applicants who failed the licensure exam three times, and licensing rules for respiratory care practitioners.

in:HB 1258.title: Crimes of violence.
in:HB 1258.summary: Rewrites and consolidates the definition of crime of violence, adds dangerous firearm possession and unlawful handgun carrying with two priors to the list, and removes the repeat violent arrestee provisions.

in:HB 1260.title: Various insurance matters.
in:HB 1260.summary: Requires reporting of suspected insurance fraud to the insurance department or the National Insurance Crime Bureau, limits liability for those reports, sets fees for claims data access, and changes property and casualty insurance guaranty rules.

in:HB 1266.title: Department of education and education matters.
in:HB 1266.summary: Makes many changes to education law, including a math teaching framework, a data science math pathway, curriculum material timelines, and salary differences for teachers with a literacy endorsement.

in:HB 1268.title: Indiana defense matters.
in:HB 1268.summary: Adds voting members and the National Guard adjutant general to the Indiana defense task force, and requires annual reports from the task force and the defense development office on spending priorities.

in:HB 1273.title: Requirements for proxy advisors.
in:HB 1273.summary: Requires proxy advisors that recommend against company management without a written financial analysis to disclose that fact clearly to the clients receiving the advice.

in:HB 1274.title: Insurance mandated gun free zone notices.
in:HB 1274.summary: Bars insurers from requiring an insured or prospective insured to post or display a gun free zone notice.

in:HB 1277.title: Health and human services matters.
in:HB 1277.summary: Requires waiver service providers to give recipients documentation to check for errors, requires certain Medicaid recipients to choose an integrated health care coordination provider, and makes other health and human services changes.

in:HB 1296.title: Mental health services.
in:HB 1296.summary: Requires the state social services secretary to certify integrated reentry and correctional support programs, and requires recovery residence owners to register with the mental health and addiction division, which must post a public list.

in:HB 1307.title: Department of child services ombudsman.
in:HB 1307.summary: Requires, rather than permits, the child services ombudsman office to hire experts and staff, investigate complaints that the department failed to protect a child or follow rules, and issue recommendations when complaints have merit.

in:HB 1342.title: County commissioner districts.
in:HB 1342.summary: Urges the legislative council to assign an interim study committee to study whether county executives should adopt certain processes for establishing or revising county commissioner districts.

in:HB 1343.title: Public safety matters.
in:HB 1343.summary: Lets the law enforcement training board hire an executive director, allows waiving some training for officers experienced in other states, raises the county jail copayment cap from $15 to $30, and requires engine cut-off switches on certain boats.

in:HB 1348.title: Regulation of grease control equipment.
in:HB 1348.summary: Sets a statewide regulatory scheme for grease control equipment, requires wastewater plants to keep accepting septage under certain circumstances, and creates a dispute process between septage haulers and treatment plants.

in:HB 1355.title: Confined feeding operations.
in:HB 1355.summary: Creates a preapplication process for approving confined feeding operations, requires refunds of application fees in some cases, exempts some operations from solid manure equipment rules, and sets requirements for earthen berms at manure storage facilities.

in:HB 1361.title: Fertilizer.
in:HB 1361.summary: Writes commercial fertilizer administrative rules into law, covering labels, registration, sampling, and containment and storage requirements for fluid and dry bulk fertilizer.

in:HB 1368.title: Carbon.
in:HB 1368.summary: Requires utilities to accept certain payment methods from the Department of Natural Resources, directs the natural resources commission to seek federal authority over Class VI wells, and sets a regulatory scheme for underground carbon dioxide storage.

in:HB 1389.title: Adoption and foster care matters.
in:HB 1389.summary: Bars governments from discriminating against people in adoption and foster care matters based on sincerely held religious belief unless required by a compelling interest, and lets them consider religious match with a child, with a right to sue.

in:HB 1408.title: Education matters.
in:HB 1408.summary: Requires Ivy Tech campuses to review building use data before capital requests and prepare strategic plans, gives the legislature access to state workforce and education data, and sets requirements and restrictions on adolescent social media use.

in:HB 1423.title: Indianapolis public education corporation.
in:HB 1423.summary: Creates the Indianapolis public education corporation and board with powers over property tax referendums and charter authorizers, and exempts Indianapolis Public Schools from building closure and transfer laws.

in:HB 1424.title: Farm and homestead food sales.
in:HB 1424.summary: Exempts homestead and small farm vendors from certain health department food-establishment rules, and bars state and local health agencies from imposing requirements beyond federal law, though they may investigate foodborne illness complaints.

in:SB 1.title: Human services matters.
in:SB 1.summary: Creates a rural health transformation fund, bars buying candy and soft drinks with SNAP benefits, ends expanded categorical SNAP eligibility, adds SNAP and Medicaid immigration-status checks, and changes Healthy Indiana Plan work requirements and copayments.

in:SB 112.title: Candidacy documents.
in:SB 112.summary: Treats the address on a candidate's notice of withdrawal as a request to update the address on the candidate's voter registration record.

in:SB 113.title: Elections matters.
in:SB 113.summary: Requires county election boards to report precinct-level results for each candidate and public question within 14 days after an election, requires the state to publish them online, and lengthens election material retention from 22 to 34 months.

in:SB 12.title: Prohibition of ranked choice voting.
in:SB 12.summary: Prohibits the use of ranked choice voting.

in:SB 160.title: Public safety.
in:SB 160.summary: Makes wearing a mask while committing a crime a sentencing aggravator, and makes it a Class A misdemeanor to put refuse on another's property intending to make the occupant reasonably fear for their physical safety.

in:SB 164.title: Study of community or urban microfarming.
in:SB 164.summary: Requires the department of agriculture to study whether to create community or urban microfarm zones statewide and report findings to the general assembly by December 1, 2027.

in:SB 176.title: Shooting ranges.
in:SB 176.summary: Bars local governments from treating shooting range building upgrades as an expansion of a nonconforming use or a ground to delay permits; makes retail sporting goods stores permitted in commercial zones and indoor ranges permitted in commercial, industrial or agricultural zones if conditions are met.

in:SB 179.title: Indiana department of transportation.
in:SB 179.summary: Lets INDOT assume federal transportation duties under certain environmental laws, changes local road and bridge grant eligibility, limits single-trip overweight truck permits, and allows the Indiana Plane Coordinate System to describe real property.

in:SB 180.title: Various health care matters.
in:SB 180.summary: Removes the 75-hour minimum and 16 classroom hours from home health aide training, changes dental hygienist education and nitrous oxide rules, and changes respiratory care practitioner licensing.

in:SB 189.title: Nonparticipating providers.
in:SB 189.summary: Requires a party requesting independent dispute resolution over out-of-network bills to notify the facility within three business days, and lets health carriers give notice and negotiate when 25 or more disputes are filed in 90 days.

in:SB 199.title: Various education matters.
in:SB 199.summary: Makes various education changes, including reports due December 1, 2026 on civic literacy and paid leave, added requirements for schools with low reading-test pass rates, and a review of accrediting agencies by the higher education commission.

in:SB 2.title: Bail procedures.
in:SB 2.summary: Makes non-murder offenses non-bailable when the state proves the evidence is strong and, by clear and convincing evidence, that the arrestee is dangerous and no release conditions would protect the public, and sets bail hearing procedures.

in:SB 200.title: Public school matters.
in:SB 200.summary: Voids certain indemnity, choice-of-law and automatic-renewal clauses in school vendor contracts made or renewed after June 30, 2026, lets youth organizations file grievances if schools deny them access to students, and requires schools that allow colleges to present to students to allow military personnel too.

in:SB 204.title: Various education matters.
in:SB 204.summary: Lets teachers licensed at charter schools seek an initial practitioner license, bars uniform academic-needs salary increases across a bargaining unit, repeals the student athlete cardiac arrest provisions, and bars requiring immunization for health-program clinical training when a parent or student objects on religious grounds.

in:SB 222.title: Family and social services administration matters.
in:SB 222.summary: Counts 9-8-8 crisis response centers and mobile crisis teams as first responders, requires certified peers to be trained by the state or an accredited body, and limits Medicaid presumptive eligibility determinations to qualified providers.

in:SB 225.title: Health matters.
in:SB 225.summary: Bars hospitals and debt collectors from collecting medical debt when the hospital is out of compliance with specified statutes, requires 60 days' notice to the health department before a hospital closes or ends a service line, and changes surgical center rules.

in:SB 226.title: Indiana department of administration.
in:SB 226.summary: Lets the Indiana department of administration use category management for state purchasing, requires an independent verification and validation program for state contracts, and requires agencies to submit annual procurement plans.

in:SB 228.title: Midwest continental divide commission.
in:SB 228.summary: Changes the Midwest continental divide commission's law so its land use and zoning plan is a plan rather than an overlay district, and addresses zoning changes or variances within half a mile of an approved trail project.

in:SB 23.title: Alcoholic beverage permits for county fairs.
in:SB 23.summary: Lets the alcohol and tobacco commission issue permits to sell alcohol on county fairgrounds run by a local board, and adds local-board events to activities allowed under existing winery, brewer, distiller and retailer permits.

in:SB 232.title: Real property appraisals.
in:SB 232.summary: Allows the city of Gary to hire an appraiser to appraise city-owned property it plans to sell, and bars city employees and officials from buying property the appraiser appraised.

in:SB 241.title: Utility service enhancement improvement costs.
in:SB 241.summary: Raises from 2,000 to 3,000 the customer count below which a water-service conservancy district may leave state utility commission jurisdiction, limits tap and capacity fees for nonprofit workforce housing, and lets water utilities adjust rates for chemical and power cost changes over 3%.

in:SB 243.title: Various tax matters.
in:SB 243.summary: Updates Indiana income tax law to match federal changes in the 2025 federal budget act, allows electronic delivery of tax department documents, extends the deadline for federal audit adjustments from 180 days to one year, and changes cigarette, petroleum severance and alcohol tax rules.

in:SB 25.title: School board candidates.
in:SB 25.summary: Sets the order in which school board candidates appear on the ballot within designated groups, listing candidates alphabetically by surname.

in:SB 261.title: Criminal vandalism.
in:SB 261.summary: Renames criminal mischief as criminal vandalism, folds institutional, cemetery, railroad and critical infrastructure mischief into it with the same penalties and defenses, and moves cave damage and refuse provisions.

in:SB 27.title: Stadium authority.
in:SB 27.summary: Creates the northwest Indiana stadium authority and board with power to finance and build a stadium using bonds, and changes Lake and Porter County food, beverage and innkeeper taxes and lets Hammond impose an admissions tax.

in:SB 270.title: Township mergers.
in:SB 270.summary: Requires the state to score township governments by performance by the end of 2026, and generally requires townships scoring four or more points to merge with another township or reorganize with a municipality, with mergers effective by January 1, 2029.

in:SB 271.title: Telecommunications wire and valuable metal dealers.
in:SB 271.summary: Adds telecommunications network wire to the definition of valuable metal for metal dealer laws, bars selling or buying it unless conditions are met, and lets people who suffer losses from violations sue for damages.

in:SB 275.title: FSSA fiscal matters.
in:SB 275.summary: Requires waiver service providers to give recipients documentation to review for errors, sets a time frame for the disability services bureau to decide requests for more service units, and creates some Medicaid reimbursement exemptions under value-based arrangements.

in:SB 277.title: Indiana department of environmental management.
in:SB 277.summary: Changes the structure and powers of the environmental management department and rules board, bars decisions based solely on unpromulgated federal risk values, and revises permitting, hearing, reporting, water pollution and waste statutes.

in:SB 285.title: Housing matters.
in:SB 285.summary: Bars camping or long-term sheltering on public land unless authorized, directs officers to assess whether emergency detention is warranted, defines gravely disabled for involuntary commitment, and sets criteria for homeless-services funding applicants.

in:SB 293.title: Pharmacist licensure.
in:SB 293.summary: Requires passing the North American Pharmacist Licensure Examination to be licensed as a pharmacist, removes an exam requirement for certain pharmacists seeking license reciprocity, and voids conflicting rules.

in:SB 3.title: Constitutional amendment ballot language.
in:SB 3.summary: Sets the ballot language for the proposed constitutional amendment concerning bail.

in:SB 4.title: Various fiscal matters.
in:SB 4.summary: Requires a fiscal impact analysis of all gubernatorial executive orders within seven days, lowers the proposed-rule cost threshold for budget committee review to $500,000, and changes community mental health center funding and reporting rules.

in:SB 56.title: Veterinary licensing.
in:SB 56.summary: Lets the board of veterinary medicine license veterinarians and registered veterinary technicians without an examination if they meet health care professional reciprocity requirements.

in:SB 6.title: Extension of water or wastewater mains.
in:SB 6.summary: Requires municipal utilities to mail written notice to affected landowners and the county plan commission, and post information online, before condemning land for water or wastewater main extensions outside city limits or the utility's service territory.

in:SB 76.title: Immigration matters.
in:SB 76.summary: Lets the attorney general defend officers, governments or colleges sued over certain immigration matters, removes the intent standard from immigration-enforcement violations, and lets the attorney general sue noncompliant governments for injunctions and civil penalties.

in:SB 80.title: Code publication.
in:SB 80.summary: Resolves amend-repeal conflicts from the 2025 session, relocates definitions chapters in alphabetical order, and updates cross-references, with no substantive change to law.

in:SB 88.title: Education matters.
in:SB 88.summary: Changes good citizenship instruction requirements, requires state colleges to accept the Classic Learning Test like the ACT or SAT for admission, and has the education department list schools offering exams to students enrolled elsewhere.

in:SB 89.title: Three-way permits.
in:SB 89.summary: Lets the alcohol and tobacco commission issue new three-way alcohol permits: three each to Schererville and Lafayette, two each to West Lafayette, Delphi and Bloomington, and eight to restaurants in a Michigan City transit district.

in:SB 91.title: Syringe exchange program.
in:SB 91.summary: Bars syringe exchange programs from operating fixed sites within 1,000 feet of specified facilities, bars providing chemical reagents or precursors, sets participation requirements, and lets the health department deny, suspend or revoke registrations for violations.

in:SB 92.title: Community corrections trust funds.
in:SB 92.summary: Lets counties running community corrections programs set up a county community corrections trust fund, with set funding sources, permitted uses, and reporting and audit requirements.

ky:HB 139.title: AN ACT relating to elections and declaring an emergency.
ky:HB 139.summary: Lets the State Board of Elections share data with other agencies to remove ineligible voters, bars buying voting systems that tabulate from barcodes or QR codes, and changes several election deadlines and procedures.

ky:HB 142.title: AN ACT relating to depredating wildlife and declaring an emergency.
ky:HB 142.summary: Sets rules for landowners, tenants and designees to take or trap wildlife damaging property, including destruction tags and 24-hour reporting, and authorizes an extra 7 to 10 day antlerless deer season in overpopulated areas.

ky:HB 567.title: AN ACT relating to open records.
ky:HB 567.summary: As introduced, lets public records custodians require a government photo ID showing an address from people requesting to inspect records, to prove Kentucky residency, and changes the definition of resident of the Commonwealth.

ky:HB 6.title: AN ACT relating to child care and declaring an emergency.
ky:HB 6.summary: Licenses child-care microcenters, requires a private third-party administrator for the Employee Child Care Assistance Partnership Program, changes the Certified Child Care Community Designation Program, and requires a child care modernization plan from the health cabinet by October 1, 2026.

ky:HB 652.title: AN ACT relating to critical facility mapping and declaring an emergency.
ky:HB 652.summary: Moves administration of the school mapping data program to the Kentucky 911 Services Board and assigns responsibility for mapping data accuracy walk-throughs.

ky:HB 669.title: AN ACT relating to child welfare.
ky:HB 669.summary: Requires the Cabinet for Health and Family Services to check whether each child in its custody gets or qualifies for Social Security or veterans benefits, and creates the Success Sequence Savings and Disbursement Plan, requiring financial training before a child accesses part of saved benefits.

ky:HB 676.title: AN ACT relating to the Kentucky statewide health data utility.
ky:HB 676.summary: Directs Legislative Research Commission staff to study creating a Kentucky statewide health data utility and report to a legislative health committee by December 1, 2026.

ky:HB 78.title: AN ACT relating to firearms liability protections and declaring an emergency.
ky:HB 78.summary: Limits civil lawsuits against firearm and ammunition makers, sellers and trade associations over criminal misuse of their products, overrides conflicting local laws, and gives the Attorney General enforcement authority.

ky:HB 869.title: AN ACT relating to fiscal matters and declaring an emergency.
ky:HB 869.summary: Creates a refundable income tax credit of up to 2.25% of wages in heritage counties, or 1.25% elsewhere, for Kentucky Business Investment Program projects, and raises skills training credit limits to $4,500 or $3,500 per trainee.

ky:SB 127.title: AN ACT relating to actuarial costs of annual leave payments in the Teachers' Retirement System.
ky:SB 127.summary: Requires the state to pay the Teachers' Retirement System's actuarial costs of school employees' annual leave accrued on or after August 1, 2026, up to 5 days a year, and limits annual leave pay in retirement benefits to employees who earned leave before then.

ky:SB 197.title: AN ACT providing funding and establishing conditions for state government agencies and institutions, making an appropriation therefor, and declaring an emergency.
ky:SB 197.summary: Amends the enacted state budget bills to add supplemental appropriations for various programs and projects, with conditions attached.

ky:SB 37.title: AN ACT relating to state symbols.
ky:SB 37.summary: Names the Treeing Walker Coonhound state dog, cats and dogs adopted from or living in Kentucky shelters or rescues official state pets, the eastern spotted skunk state nongame mammal, and the eastern hellbender state amphibian.

ky:SB 59.title: AN ACT relating to prohibited uses of tax dollars and resources.
ky:SB 59.summary: Bars government entities, including school districts, from using tax dollars or other resources to advocate for or against a public question on the ballot. Sets fines, with a third or later violation a Class A misdemeanor; exempts educational television and employees acting on their own time.

ky:SB 65.title: AN ACT relating to deficient administrative regulations and declaring an emergency.
ky:SB 65.summary: Nullifies administrative regulations found deficient in the 2026 session, covering Medicaid outpatient pharmacy, tobacco and vapor licenses, online insurance verification, controlled substance monitoring, and kin caregiver services. Takes effect immediately as an emergency.

ky:SB 9.title: AN ACT relating to housing districts.
ky:SB 9.summary: Lets local governments create residential infrastructure districts funded by bonds and special property assessments, and housing development districts that can waive zoning after a hearing and pay incentive payments to developers. Limits housing districts to 20% agricultural land.

ky:SB 98.title: AN ACT relating to welding safety.
ky:SB 98.summary: Requires projects using structural steel welding to hire a certified welder and meet national welding standards, effective January 1, 2027. Exempts welding on the premises of a homeowner or farmer.

la:HB 1005.title: INDIGENT DEFENSE: Provides relative to the office of the state public defender (EN NO IMPACT   See Note)
la:HB 1005.summary: Replaces references to the Louisiana Public Defender Board with the office of the state public defender, whom the governor appoints with Senate confirmation to a two-year term. District public defenders who contract with the office are independent contractors.

la:HB 1007.title: DISTRICTS/SPECIAL: Creates the Faubourg Nouveau Marigny Improvement District in Orleans Parish
la:HB 1007.summary: Creates the Faubourg Nouveau Marigny Improvement District in Orleans Parish, run by a five-member board, to fund beautification and streetscape projects. Allows a voter-approved parcel fee, such as up to $100 a year for improved residential parcels.

la:HB 1018.title: ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGE PERMT: Provides relative to limitations on the issuance of certain alcoholic beverage permits
la:HB 1018.summary: Bars new high and low alcohol permits for small premises under 5,000 square feet in Louisiana House District 2 from August 1, 2026 through 2027. Exempts downtown Shreveport, Bossier City and purchases of existing licensed premises.

la:HB 1028.title: MEDICAID: Requires the Louisiana Department of Health to increase the reimbursement rates for nonemergency medical transportation providers (EN +$2,601,174 GF EX See Note)
la:HB 1028.summary: Requires the Department of Health to set Medicaid non-emergency medical transportation rates of at least $14.50 per trip and $2.10 per mile, with a multi-passenger rate method. Limits rides outside the home or neighboring parishes unless medically necessary.

la:HB 1029.title: ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGE PERMT: Provides relative to limitations on the issuance of certain alcoholic beverage permits
la:HB 1029.summary: Extends the ban on new high-alcohol permits in Louisiana House District 3 through 2027 and bans new low-alcohol permits there through 2032. Exempts national chains, defined as companies operating in 10 or more states.

la:HB 1052.title: CHILDRENS CODE: Provides relative to confidentiality policies and procedures pertaining to work product created, received, or maintained by child advocacy centers and multidisciplinary investigative teams
la:HB 1052.summary: Requires each multidisciplinary child abuse investigative team and child advocacy center to adopt a written confidentiality policy limiting shared information to authorized participants for investigation, assessment, prosecution and treatment, and covers team work product.

la:HB 1082.title: CIVIL/VENUE: Provides for venue with respect to the Municipal Police Employees' Retirement System
la:HB 1082.summary: Changes where lawsuits involving the Municipal Police Employees' Retirement System are filed: in East Baton Rouge or its domicile parish when it is the defendant, and where the claim arises when it is the plaintiff.

la:HB 1084.title: STUDENT/TUITION: Provides relative to tuition and mandatory fees for public postsecondary education institutions
la:HB 1084.summary: Authorizes each public college and university to set and adjust tuition and fees for all programs, with increases capped at 10% per year and no cap on reductions, starting January 1, 2027.

la:HB 1098.title: LIABILITY/CIVIL: Provides with respect to a limitation of liability for aerospace entities
la:HB 1098.summary: Bars nuisance, trespass and similar claims against aerospace flight entities that own at least 20,000 contiguous acres in Louisiana, over noise, vibration, light, exhaust and other flight-related disturbances. Exceptions include gross negligence and violating federal license conditions.

la:HB 1117.title: INSURANCE: Provides relative to certain insurer contractual payments and prescriptive period
la:HB 1117.summary: Provides that an insurer's payment on certain insurance claims is not an acknowledgment of debt and does not extend the time limit to sue. Requires written notice of this with unconditional payments on homeowners' dwelling and other structures claims.

la:HB 1189.title: WILDLIFE & FISHERIES: Provides for charter boat fishing guide licenses
la:HB 1189.summary: Requires freshwater charter boat fishing guides operating on U.S. waters in Louisiana to hold a U.S. Coast Guard captain's license, and renames the nonresident saltwater guide license a nonresident charter boat fishing guide license.

la:HB 1193.title: CONTRACTS/BIDS: Provides for Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity construction phase contracts (EN SEE FISC NOTE SD EX See Note)
la:HB 1193.summary: Lets the Coastal Protection and Restoration Authority award indefinite delivery, indefinite quantity construction contracts for coastal protection projects, using single or multiple awards and low bid, best value or qualification-based selection.

la:HB 1194.title: AGRICULTURAL COMMODITIES: Provides with respect to the Healthy Food Retail Act (EN NO IMPACT   See Note)
la:HB 1194.summary: Expands the Healthy Food Retail Act to cover food deserts, defined as low-income census tracts with many residents far from a supermarket, and other food access projects, with priority for projects showing demand and long-term sustainability.

la:HB 1195.title: AMUSEMENTS/SPORTS: Provides relative to the Louisiana State Athletic Commission
la:HB 1195.summary: Changes State Athletic Commission rules: cuts the maximum rounds in a boxing contest from 20 to 12, raises the maximum fine on licensees from $1,000 to $5,000 and on unauthorized events from $500 to $5,000, and adds cease and desist authority.

la:HB 1201.title: ELECTED OFFICIALS/COMP: Provides with respect to the compensation of statewide elected officials and legislators (EN INCREASE GF EX See Note)
la:HB 1201.summary: Lets legislators claim per diem and mileage for up to 10 days a month of official business, extends the $1,000 monthly housing allowance to all legislators, and adds inflation adjustments and allowances for statewide elected officials other than the governor.

la:HB 1203.title: EDUCATION: Provides relative to parent-driven learning microschools
la:HB 1203.summary: Defines parent-driven learning microschools as parent groups teaching mixed-age children in homes or community spaces. Provides that using a building for one does not change its zoning, building code or fire safety status, and exempts microschools from state registration and early learning center licensing.

la:HB 1243.title: SEWERAGE/N O WATER BD: Provides relative to the Sewerage and Water Board of New Orleans
la:HB 1243.summary: Removes the state-law makeup of the New Orleans Sewerage and Water Board, including its selection committee and quorum rule, and lets the board's composition follow the city charter, with the city council setting appointment and term rules by ordinance.

la:HB 1256.title: PROPERTY/UNCLAIMED: Provides with respect to abandoned digital assets
la:HB 1256.summary: Adds digital assets to the unclaimed property law, presuming them abandoned after three years without owner contact or returned mail. Requires holders to warn owners that the asset may be liquidated if they do not respond.

la:HB 153.title: COURTS/CRIMINAL: Provides with respect to the collection of criminal court fines and fees
la:HB 153.summary: Bars reporting criminal fines and fees debt to credit bureaus or consumer reporting agencies. Does not apply to traffic law violations under Title 32 or municipal law violations. Takes effect August 1, 2026.

la:HB 210.title: ETHICS/CODE: Provides for restrictions on payments from nonpublic sources
la:HB 210.summary: Bars statewide elected officials from being paid for lobbying, consulting or advising. Applies retroactively an existing exception letting school board and local governing authority members work for employers doing business with their government, except where an ethics body has issued a final decision.

la:HB 211.title: COURTS: Provides relative to the creation, administration, and eligibility requirements of the Homelessness Court program (EN SEE FISC NOTE GF EX)
la:HB 211.summary: Lets district courts create Homelessness Court programs with probation conditions, and creates the crime of unauthorized camping on public property, punishable by up to $500, six months in jail, or both. Offenders may qualify for court programs.

la:HB 325.title: TOPS: Provides relative to TOPS-Tech (EN INCREASE GF EX See Note)
la:HB 325.summary: Lets part-time students receive TOPS awards in some cases. For TOPS-Tech, adds a third eligibility criterion of nine early college credit hours, and students qualify by meeting two of three criteria, for 2026-2027 graduates onward.

la:HB 398.title: PUBLIC OFFLS/EMPS: Prohibits payment for meals and incidental expenses for state public officials and employees from exceeding amounts for such expenses established by the U.S. General Services Administration
la:HB 398.summary: Caps reimbursement for meals and incidental expenses of judicial, legislative and executive branch officers and employees at the U.S. General Services Administration daily maximum rates, with an allowance for agency-hosted conferences and working meals.

la:HB 399.title: CRIMINAL/PROCEDURE: Provides relative to temporary release of inmates for limited purposes (EN SEE FISC NOTE GF EX)
la:HB 399.summary: Extends from 60 to 120 days the expected time of death that lets the corrections secretary grant temporary release to an inmate with a terminal illness for palliative or medical care. Takes effect August 1, 2026.

la:HB 410.title: CIVIL/PROCEDURE: Requires notification of all parties to record in-person communication
la:HB 410.summary: Bars using wearable video-recording eyeglasses to record or transcribe a conversation unless all participants are notified. Exempts public meetings, law enforcement and emergencies, recording evidence for legal proceedings, and recordings made by a participant in their own home or business.

la:HB 414.title: HEALTH: Provides for prohibitions on hiring individuals with certain criminal convictions
la:HB 414.summary: Requires background checks on anyone owning or managing a therapeutic group home, removes licensed ambulance personnel from hiring bans for criminal offenses, and lets hospitals run criminal history checks through accredited consumer reporting agencies.

la:HB 420.title: CHILDREN/DCFS: Requires the Department of Children and Family Services to obtain background checks on all employees (EN INCREASE GF EX See Note)
la:HB 420.summary: Requires the Department of Children and Family Services to run criminal background checks and state central registry searches on all current and prospective employees, not only those in child-facing roles, and extends the termination rule for registry matches.

la:HB 459.title: ELECTIONS/CANDIDATES: Provides relative to the use of artificial intelligence in political campaigns
la:HB 459.summary: Bars electioneering communications showing AI-altered images, likenesses or voices of candidates that falsely appear authentic, unless clearly labeled as AI-created. Penalties apply only when done with intent to injure a candidate's reputation or deceive voters. Exempts broadcasters with no control over content.

la:HB 481.title: PUBLIC PRINTING: Provides for the cost of publishing official proceedings and public notices
la:HB 481.summary: Raises the maximum rate parishes, municipalities and school boards may pay by contract to publish official proceedings and public notices to three cents per character in all parishes, up from two cents or one and a half cents.

la:HB 538.title: COURTS/JUVENILE: Provides relative to the judicial expense fund for the Juvenile Court for the parish of East Baton Rouge
la:HB 538.summary: Raises the maximum additional civil filing fee for the East Baton Rouge Juvenile Court judicial expense fund from $15 to $45 and gives the judges sitting together, rather than the chief judge, control of the fee and fund.

la:HB 593.title: MTR VEHICLE/OFFICE: Increases the maximum service and transaction fee a governing authority may assess to fund an office of motor vehicles field office not fully funded by the state (EN +$1,540,000 LF RV See Note)
la:HB 593.summary: Raises the maximum local fee per transaction at Office of Motor Vehicles field offices to $8 statewide, up from $4.50 and higher caps in a few places, with Shreveport field offices exempt. Takes effect August 1, 2026.

la:HB 608.title: ATHLETICS: Provides relative to the confidentiality of documents related to an intercollegiate athletics revenue sharing program
la:HB 608.summary: Makes the total revenue a college spends on athlete revenue sharing public, but keeps confidential each athlete's payment, each sport's allocation, and negotiation records. Applies to past and pending records requests.

la:HB 690.title: EDUCATION: Provides relative to education service providers and vendors of educational products (EN NO IMPACT   See Note)
la:HB 690.summary: Bars education agencies from knowingly contracting with education service providers or vendors that are foreign adversaries, foreign terrorist organizations or their agents, and bars subcontracting with them. Requires notifying the attorney general and suspending payments pending review.

la:HB 719.title: DISTRICT ATTORNEYS/ASST: Provides relative to the number of assistant district attorneys in each judicial district (EN +$3,411,000 GF EX See Note)
la:HB 719.summary: Raises the number of assistant district attorneys authorized in most judicial districts, for example from 55 to 71 in the 19th and from 30 to 44 in the 22nd, and leaves several districts unchanged.

la:HB 723.title: MTR VEHICLE/MOTORCYCLES: Authorizes drivers of certain two-wheeled vehicles to proceed through a red light under certain circumstances
la:HB 723.summary: Lets drivers of motorcycles, mopeds and bicycles proceed through a red light at a vehicle-actuated signal after stopping for two full cycles or two minutes, treating it as a stop sign, and yielding to pedestrians and cross traffic.

la:HB 730.title: AIRCRAFT/AVIATION: Provides relative to the use of automatic dependent surveillance-broadcast systems (EN SEE FISC NOTE LF RV)
la:HB 730.summary: Bars using aircraft tracking data from ADS-B systems as a basis for charging fees or taxes to owners of aircraft of 12,499 pounds or less operating in the state.

la:HB 732.title: MTR VEHICLE/OFFICE: Provides for a temporary waiver of fees for final delinquent debt based on special circumstances (EN DECREASE SG RV See Note)
la:HB 732.summary: Lets the motor vehicles commissioner pause fines, fees and license suspensions for up to 30 days so a person can get life-sustaining medicine or treatment. Suspends the road usage fee on non-plug-in hybrids until August 1, 2027.

la:HB 75.title: GAMING: Creates an enhanced promotional play pilot program relative to net slot machine proceeds (EN -$574,627 GF RV See Note)
la:HB 75.summary: Creates a pilot program, July 2026 through June 2027, raising the promotional play wagers racing-facility slot licensees may offer from $5 million to $7 million. Requires licensees to report the effect on proceeds, fees and taxes by March 1, 2027.

la:HB 750.title: CONSUMERS/PROTECTION: Provides for cancellation of automatic renewal subscriptions
la:HB 750.summary: Creates the Click-to-Cancel Act, requiring businesses with automatic renewal subscriptions to disclose terms clearly, get affirmative consent, send an acknowledgment, keep consent records for a year, and offer an easy, timely cancellation method.

la:HB 769.title: DOMESTIC ABUSE: Provides relative to the removal authority process with respect to domestic offenders
la:HB 769.summary: Lets courts hold a person charged with certain domestic abuse offenses without bail for a 48 to 72 hour cooling-off period, considering any increased risk to the victim, family or public. The period runs within the 72-hour limit for first appearance.

la:HB 775.title: HEALTH/CHILDREN: Provides relative to minor's consent for medical procedures and treatments
la:HB 775.summary: Requires parental or guardian consent before health care providers treat a person under the age of majority, replacing prior law letting minors consent. Lists exceptions, including military service, emancipation, pregnancy care, substance misuse treatment, and sexually transmitted disease treatment.

la:HB 804.title: ENERGY: Creates the Louisiana Energy Protection Act (EN NO IMPACT   See Note)
la:HB 804.summary: Bars lawsuits in Louisiana courts seeking damages for climate change from greenhouse gas emissions, except claims over violations of emission laws, permit terms or certain federal workplace safety standards.

la:HB 848.title: MTR VEHICLE/DEALERS: Provides with respect to all terrain vehicle dealerships
la:HB 848.summary: Adds golf carts to the all-terrain vehicle dealer law, covers any retailer selling them, and requires such dealers to have adequate facilities to support warranty service, maintenance and repair of the vehicles they sell.

la:HB 864.title: HIGHWAYS: Authorizes municipalities to establish fire limits and to prohibit the storage, placement, accumulation, abandonment, or use of certain materials within the right-of-way of certain public structures
la:HB 864.summary: Lets municipalities set fire limits and bar storing or using flammable, explosive or combustible material above ground in the right-of-way of public bridges, overpasses and tunnels. Violations carry fines up to $1,000, with exceptions for permitted events and utilities.

la:HB 951.title: LABOR: Creates the office of business workforce solutions within Louisiana Works (EN INCREASE GF EX See Note)
la:HB 951.summary: Creates the office of business workforce solutions within Louisiana Works, adds duties for the Workforce Investment Council, and treats employer outreach spending for the Incumbent Worker Training Program as non-administrative expense.

la:HB 953.title: PLUMBERS: Provides relative to plumbing licenses
la:HB 953.summary: Abolishes the State Plumbing Board and moves plumber and gas fitter licensing to a new Plumbing Contractors Subcommittee of the State Licensing Board for Contractors, adding two board members from plumbing industry groups.

la:HB 956.title: FIRE PROTECT/FIRE MARSHAL: Provides relative to fireworks
la:HB 956.summary: Changes fireworks rules: limits retail sales to 1.4G-class fireworks, starts sale hours at 7 a.m., adds Memorial Day and Labor Day sale windows, repeals Class C public displays, and raises pyrotechnic operator license fees to $200 new and $100 renewal.

la:HB 971.title: MEDICAID: Provides relative to Medicaid reimbursement for rural health clinics (EN +$2,655,159 GF EX See Note)
la:HB 971.summary: Requires the Department of Health to equalize Medicaid rates between independent and provider-based rural health clinics, raising the independent clinic encounter rate subject to federal approval. Adds rural health clinics to facility need review and requires monthly encounter and spending reports.

la:HB 989.title: MOTOR VEHICLES: Modifies charges collected by public license tag agents
la:HB 989.summary: Raises the maximum convenience charge and the registration reinstatement fee that public license tag agents may collect from $23 to $27.

la:SB 237.title: CHILDREN: Provides relative to child welfare. (8/1/26) (EN NO IMPACT   See Note)
la:SB 237.summary: Changes child welfare notification and oversight: requires notice of child abuse deaths to legislative leaders and committee chairs, requires reporting of deaths and near-fatalities to the child ombudsman, and gives the ombudsman remote access to state child-services systems.

la:SB 268.title: LOCAL FINANCE: Provides for lead service line replacement. (8/1/26)
la:SB 268.summary: Lets municipalities adopt ordinances allowing city water systems to enter private property to replace lead service lines after at least seven days' notice, except in emergencies. Entry is limited to the replacement work.

la:SB 283.title: SPECIAL DISTRICTS: Creates the BLVD at Harding Area Special District in the city of Baton Rouge. (gov sig)
la:SB 283.summary: Creates two special districts in Baton Rouge, the BLVD at Harding Area district and a Baton Rouge Community College economic development district, each run by a board with power to issue bonds. Extends tax increment financing authority to the Harding district.

la:SB 384.title: TECHNOLOGY: Authorizes creation of the Pilot Innovation Hub. (8/1/26) (EN SEE FISC NOTE LF EX See Note)
la:SB 384.summary: Lets parishes designate themselves Pilot Innovation Hubs, where local governments may contract with a pilot innovation contractor to test new technologies, using public property and aligned permitting and zoning.

la:SB 387.title: HEALTH/ACC INSURANCE: Provides relative to pharmacy benefit managers. (1/1/27) (EN INCREASE SG EX See Note)
la:SB 387.summary: Regulates pharmacy benefit managers: limits their pay to flat fees, bars keeping rebates and spread pricing, and allows annual audits. Sets a $25,000 civil penalty per violation, with license suspension or revocation if not corrected within 30 days.

la:SB 406.title: TAX/LOCAL: Authorizes the city of Slidell to levy a hotel occupancy tax. (gov sig) (EN +$590,000 LF RV See Note)
la:SB 406.summary: Lets the city of Slidell, with voter approval, levy a hotel occupancy tax of up to 2% of room charges, with proceeds funding recreational facilities or tourism initiatives named in the tax proposition.

la:SB 433.title: MEDICAID: Provides for Medicaid coverage of certain medications. (1/1/27) (EN +$3,000,000 GF EX See Note)
la:SB 433.summary: Requires Medicaid to cover medically necessary, FDA-approved weight loss medications for recipients who meet Department of Health criteria. Allows prior authorization, bars step therapy, and takes effect upon legislative appropriation.

la:SB 444.title: EXPROPRIATION: Provides relative to expropriation by the city of St. George. (gov sig)
la:SB 444.summary: Lets the city of St. George take property by expropriation for public projects such as streets, drainage, utilities and flood protection, using the same procedures as the Department of Transportation and Development, including taking before judgment.

la:SB 449.title: PUBLIC CONTRACTS: Provides for the procurement of materials and goods. (8/1/26)
la:SB 449.summary: Exempts political subdivisions that own or operate a railroad from public bid requirements when buying used locomotives, rolling stock, track maintenance equipment and their parts. Takes effect August 1, 2026.

la:SB 479.title: JUDGES: Provides for legislative address to the governor for the removal of certain judges for malfeasance, gross misconduct, or incompetence committed while in office. (See Act)
la:SB 479.summary: Sets procedures for impeaching state officials and judges, including a defined "gross misconduct" standard, sworn citizen complaints, and a joint legislative investigating committee with subpoena power. Lets the House impeach by majority vote.

la:SB 513.title: PUBLIC CONTRACTS: Provides for public works project delivery methods. (8/1/26)
la:SB 513.summary: Lets public airports use design-build contracting for vertical facilities such as workforce training buildings, control towers, parking garages and hangars, excluding commercial airport passenger terminals and equipment. Takes effect August 1, 2026.

md:HB 1118.title: Health, Health Insurance, and Health Occupations - Perinatal Behavioral Health Conditions
md:HB 1118.summary: Requires Medicaid and insurers, from January 1, 2027, to cover screening for perinatal behavioral health conditions such as postpartum depression. Requires providers to screen at well visits in a child's first year and the health department to identify screening tools.

md:HB 1137.title: Residential-in-Commercial-Zone Laws - Study (Bring Back Main Street Act)
md:HB 1137.summary: Requires the Department of Housing and Community Development to study laws requiring local governments to allow residential or mixed-use development on commercially zoned lots, and report by December 1, 2026.

md:HB 1151.title: Maryland Department of Health - Study on Maryland Medical Assistance Program Reimbursement of Hospice Room and Board Services
md:HB 1151.summary: Requires the Health Care Commission and Medicaid to study the effects of Medicaid paying for hospice house room and board, including costs, savings and hospital use, with a report to legislative committees by December 1, 2026.

md:HB 1216.title: Insurance – Certificates of Guarantee for County Bond Requirements – All Counties
md:HB 1216.summary: Lets all counties, not only some, accept certificates of guarantee from certain associations or contractors to meet county bond requirements.

md:HB 1243.title: Prince George's County - Personal Property Tax Exemption for Small Manufacturers PG 423-26
md:HB 1243.summary: Exempts personal property of small manufacturers holding an alcoholic beverages manufacturer's license, with 50 or fewer employees, from municipal personal property tax in Prince George's County, for tax years beginning after June 30, 2026.

md:HB 1286.title: Anne Arundel County - Alcoholic Beverages - Barbershop and Beauty Salon License
md:HB 1286.summary: Lets Anne Arundel County barbershop and beauty salon license holders serve each customer up to 1.7 ounces of liquor per visit for on-premises consumption, in addition to beer and wine.

md:HB 1300.title: African American Heritage Preservation Program and Maryland Commission for Women - Renaming and Alterations
md:HB 1300.summary: Renames the African American Heritage Preservation Program for Speaker Adrienne A. Jones, makes the Maryland Commission for Women's executive director a skilled service state employee rather than a Secretary appointee, and changes the commission's duties.

md:HB 1321.title: Child Care Scholarship Program - Application Process and Copays - Alterations
md:HB 1321.summary: Requires the State Department of Education to help Child Care Scholarship applicants who qualify for public prekindergarten or Head Start enroll in those programs while a waitlist exists, and limits certain copays.

md:HB 1335.title: Department of Information Technology - Information Technology Staffing and Capability Assessment - Independent Study
md:HB 1335.summary: Requires the Department of Information Technology to hire an outside party to study IT and cybersecurity staffing and workforce alignment in the State, and submit the study by November 1, 2027.

md:HB 1430.title: Maryland Public Charter School Program - School Facilities - Funding
md:HB 1430.summary: Requires the Governor, from fiscal 2028, to budget capital improvement funds for public charter school facilities equal to prior-year charter enrollment times $200, distributed directly to schools by the Interagency Commission on School Construction.

md:HB 1434.title: Maryland Department of Health - Caregiver Resource Webpage - Establishment
md:HB 1434.summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to create and maintain a webpage of information and resources for caregivers.

md:HB 1466.title: Department of Housing and Community Development - Appraisal Gap From Historic Redlining Financial Assistance Program - Qualified Properties
md:HB 1466.summary: Expands the definition of a qualified property under the Appraisal Gap From Historic Redlining Financial Assistance Program.

md:HB 1470.title: Medical Assistance Programs - Drug Dispensing - Cost-of-Dispensing Survey
md:HB 1470.summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to conduct its in-State drug cost-of-dispensing survey for Medicaid at least every 3 years, starting in 2026, and report results to the General Assembly by December 1 of survey years.

md:HB 1490.title: Family Investment Program - Temporary Cash Assistance - Good Cause and Adequate Reason Exceptions
md:HB 1490.summary: Bars the Department of Human Services from denying or cutting temporary cash assistance when a person has good cause for not cooperating with child support, and defines good cause as cooperation possibly harming the child.

md:HB 1587.title: Gaming - Operation of Electronic Instant Bingo Machines and Report by State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency
md:HB 1587.summary: Raises from 54 to 100 the bingo cards a handheld device may play at once under the slot machine definition, lets electronic instant bingo machines skip paper tickets unless the player asks, and requires a state report on expanding them by December 1, 2026.

md:HB 161.title: Property Tax Credit - Retail Service Station Conversions
md:HB 161.summary: Lets Baltimore City and counties or municipalities grant a property tax credit on land converted from a retail gas station to other uses, only if underground storage tanks have been permanently closed.

md:HB 191.title: Consumer Protection - Retail Transactions for Essential Consumer Goods - Cash Payments
md:HB 191.summary: Bars merchants from refusing cash, requiring cards, or charging cash payers more for essential goods such as food, medicine and fuel in in-person sales under $300 between 6 a.m. and 10 p.m. Violations count as unfair or deceptive trade practices.

md:HB 200.title: Sale of Residential Real Property - Required Flood Risk Disclosure
md:HB 200.summary: Requires the Department of the Environment to create a flood risk disclosure form, and from July 1, 2027 requires sellers of certain homes to give buyers a completed form before signing a sale contract.

md:HB 2100.title: Election Districts - General Assembly and Representatives in Congress
md:HB 2100.summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment, for the November 2026 ballot, stating that the state constitution provides no criteria for congressional district boundaries, limits legislative district requirements to state House and Senate districts, and lets the legislature give the Supreme Court original jurisdiction over congressional maps.

md:HB 2101.title: Arbitration Reform for State Employees Act of 2026 - Withdraw and Repeal of Duplicate Proposed Constitutional Amendment
md:HB 2101.summary: Repeals a duplicate proposed constitutional amendment on collective bargaining for State employees, so only one copy appears on the November 2026 ballot. An identical amendment in another act stays on the ballot. Takes effect immediately as an emergency.

md:HB 211.title: Baltimore County – Property Tax Credit – Fraternal Order of Police Lodge 34
md:HB 211.summary: Lets Baltimore County grant a property tax credit on certain real property owned by Fraternal Order of Police Lodge 34, for tax years after June 30, 2026.

md:HB 306.title: Vehicle Laws - Manufacturers and Dealers - Prices Listed on Dealer Websites (Jack Fitzgerald Price Transparency Act)
md:HB 306.summary: Bars vehicle manufacturers from penalizing a dealer for stating on its website that an advertised price is the manufacturer's minimum advertised price and that the dealer may offer a lower price.

md:HB 315.title: Landlord and Tenant - Discrimination in Housing for Income-Based Housing Subsidies and Positive Rental History Reporting
md:HB 315.summary: Bars landlords from refusing to rent to prospective tenants who use income-based housing subsidies, and from using credit history from before the subsidy, with exceptions. Violations are discriminatory housing practices. Requires offering to report tenants' positive rent payment history.

md:HB 326.title: Education - Maryland Center for School Safety - Anonymous Reporting System
md:HB 326.summary: Requires the Maryland Center for School Safety to run an anonymous system for reporting school or student safety concerns, and requires each local school system to participate, with reports kept from public inspection.

md:HB 330.title: Maryland Legal Services Corporation - Board of Directors - Membership
md:HB 330.summary: Increases the Maryland Legal Services Corporation Board of Directors from 9 to 12 members.

md:HB 396.title: Residential Child Care Programs - Education of Children and Training of Child and Youth Care Practitioners
md:HB 396.summary: Requires residential child care programs to keep children age 5 and older enrolled in their prior school unless a social services department decides otherwise, and sets requirements for approved training programs for residential child and youth care practitioners. Takes effect January 1, 2027.

md:HB 457.title: Institutions of Higher Education - Provision of Menstrual Hygiene Products - Requirement
md:HB 457.summary: Requires colleges that offer on-campus housing to provide free menstrual hygiene products in all student health centers by August 1, 2028.

md:HB 497.title: Family Law - Temporary and Final Protective Orders - Duration
md:HB 497.summary: Lengthens temporary protective orders from up to 7 days after service to up to 14 days after issuance, and requires the final protective order hearing within 14 days after the temporary order is issued.

md:HB 529.title: Code Revision - Health - Maryland Medical Assistance Program
md:HB 529.summary: Revises, restates and recodifies the State's laws on the Maryland Medical Assistance Program.

md:HB 548.title: Land Use - Permitting - Development Rights (Maryland Housing Certainty Act)
